Rick Bott,  Cairn Indian Limited - Chief Operating Officer: Good morning, everybody. It's good to see some familiar faces out there. It's been a while since I've been up here visiting, and longer since you guys came out and visited, but I think if you remember back when we talked out there in Barmer, I said one of the critical challenges for us at that time was to get our organization focused and be able to  and that focus has been singularly on execution and delivery.
 Hopefully, as we go through the presentation today, you'll be able  the pictures will give you a flavor of the progress we've made to date with that focus.
 I've got an overview slide here for you for the project, for those of you who aren't aware of it; but most of you are aware of what the project is. But I really want to cover four key points for you today.
 The first key point is that we stand on the verge. Train 1 is ready to go; Trains 2, 3 and the pipeline. We're targeting for the first half of 2010 to build the capacity for the production plateau for Mangala of 125,000 barrels a day that we talked about before, with an eventual plateau target of 175,000 barrels a day in 2011.
 The third key point is that it's taken us to the point of being ready to produce to be able to de-risk the oil price and the volume off-take from the nominated buyers.
 And finally, we'd like to cover some of the tangible actions that we're doing; actions and programs on the ground that we're doing to unlock the future value of the potential in Rajasthan.
 For those of you who've been involved in the development, or following the story since inception, I think the Mangala area and the Rajasthan Basin really proved the old E&P adage that big fields get bigger. I think, as we continue to work through and gain additional data about the subsurface, we've been continually impressed and surprised on the upside; developing additional production capacity as a result of that links the surface facilities to our objectives from the subsurface.
 And so, as we've continued to progress, we've tried to build and  design and build an infrastructure around a couple of key elements. One of those is strategic control of the infrastructure through the production-sharing contract, and secondly, is building the capacity for growth.
 So the operational flexibility that Bill continues to talk about has been translated into the vision of what production capacity we have, and the infrastructure that's required in the field. And so that starts with the subsurface completion techniques, the heater strings going through to the well pads, the drilling rigs, the infield flow lines, the separation facilities and, of course, the export infrastructure.
 So to fill that eventual capacity, there's a couple things that we're doing. I'm going to show you just a couple slides on the near term plans that we have to unlock that potential.
 First of all, there's the discovered resource, and we show you a ramp  a schematic ramp-up profile to show you that where we sit now in Q3 2009, where we talked to you about as our forecast from back in February, we're very much still focused on delivering now Trains 2, Trains 3 and the pipeline, to be able to reach that production plateau.
 However, there are several other areas where we see subsurface potential that gives us the optionality that Bill talked about for future growth and/or to extend the plateau or enhance that plateau. That comes from the EOR, which we'll talk about here shortly, Barmer Hill exploration and the exploitation of the 22 discoveries that have been made.
 So the discovered resource, the primary driver, is the EOR and Barmer Hill. In the EOR, we're essentially come through our preparatory phase. We're now designing the facilities, and we're designing the wells, both the producers and the injectors. That's then translating into action phase. Now we're getting ready to start tendering for the services and for the facilities, as well as putting that all together into an operational efficiency model where we're trying to look at combining that with the Barmer Hill, the exploration drilling, to put together a rig program for 2010. So we anticipate starting the pilot program for the EOR late this quarter, or first quarter of 2010.
 So the other two areas that we think we see where there's a material difference to be made is the Barmer Hill discovered resource. If you remember, that's a tight reservoir, low permeability reservoir, an unconventional reservoir that sits above the main reservoir, the Fatehgarh.
 You combine that unconventional tight reservoir with the waxy crude, and there are quite a number of challenges, technical and operational challenges, for us to try to experiment with and address. And so we're getting ready to do a pilot program, again, tied to a rig program with the EOR, where we can go out in the field and re-enter some of the wells that have already been  we have discovered behind [Paipai], and look at testing some of the stimulation and completion techniques that have been used successfully in North America to see if we can find the right mix of operational efficiencies to be able to scale that up to commercial production in the future.
 Based on the results of that, we've got additional wells to test, and we'll go out and look at drilling, testing and coring some additional wells in some other areas. We're mainly going to focus on Mangala and Aishwariya to start with, but then we'll move out into other areas, and that will include some horizontal wells and horizontal fracs.
 The whole goal there is to get to full field development planning in 2011, so that hopefully, the implementation can correlate with the implementation of the full field EOR in 2013/2014.
 Then going to exploration potential, we've embarked this year on a much more detailed reevaluation of the basin. That's been really focusing on using some new technologies, as well as a play-based exploration approach looking for new plays, new ideas.
 We're encouraged by what we see so far, and that's now going to translate into work in the field. That work will consist of additional 3D seismic, some depth imaging, and then, of course, getting into drilling.
 We're focusing  in exploration, we're really focusing in on the Raageshwari East area, where we had a discovery there last year. That's now been renamed the Tukaram field. So we'll be drilling some appraisal wells on that, as well as drilling some other trap types and some other play types in and around that Raageshwari area.
 So that will be the near term exploration focus. Again, that's tied in in a rig program we're designing now with EOR and with Barmer Hill.
 I think also the key point for  just to link back to that infrastructure slide, I think the key point there is that now is the opportunity  we're getting into the next level of detail in the basin, and it's an opportunity for us to leverage the infrastructure investment that we've had. But I think also the key takeaway is that we're going to be drilling new ideas in this basin for a long time to come.
 So if I shift gears now, I'd like to give you a little bit of an overview on the project.
 Train 1, as we've talked about, is ready. I'm going to show you some pictures in a moment. The key elements to start production are in place. The preparation for Trains 2/Trains 3 are ongoing. The work there is really broken down into area-wise and then system and sub-system type approaches. We have teams that are responsible for all the systems in that area with responsibility for the delivery of that. Things are going well; we're moving  we're progressing well, and it's just a question of continuing to keep that execution focused.
 Shifting down a little bit, talking about the subsurface, we really have  we've talked about the rigs, we've talked about the technology being employed, we've talked about all the efforts that we're doing there, and we can continue to report well statistics for you.
 I think the key takeaways from the subsurface are a couple of points. Firstly, we really started all of our drilling, our development drilling, in the southern part of the field, where we actually had the most uncertainty about the reservoir deliverability.
 The good news is that both of the reservoir systems there, the upper Fatehgarh and the lower Fatehgarh, are quite different, but they're both world-class type reservoirs. And the good thing is that the reservoirs are in line with our expectations. We've drilled on four well pads in the South. Now we're moving up to the center part of the field where we have a lot more control and a lot less uncertainty, and again, the reservoirs are meeting expectations.
 We're also drilling in the Raageshwari area. Those wells  we're just starting a campaign there; we've got two wells drilled. And now, as we start to get into production and start to flow oil, we're going to be able to move into drilling and completing our horizontal wells, which are much higher rate deliverability.
 I think the key takeaway from the drilling and the subsurface is that we'll have plenty of well head capacity and we won't be deliverability-constrained.
 So I like to tease my delivery manager for the production for Train 1. He gets very, very excited when he's out there and, as you can see, he's got a bunch of shiny new toys. They're now installed; they're ready to go. Heated storage, pumping and valves, all the completion and the loading bays are there ready to go, as Bill said, for the inauguration and hopefully commencement of production at the end of the month.
 So a couple of other pictures, just to give you the scope and the scale of the upstream; I think it is a project on really a massive scale. And this slide I just put up there to show you, it's really about what we've achieved to date.
 When you're out there, I think you've got a perception how remote the area is, and how unusual this large production plant is sitting in the middle of a desert. What you couldn't get a feel for was the hostile environment.
 Well, having gone out there this summer, with temperatures in excess of 50 degrees every day, it's really, really a tough environment. When dust storms come through, it's a hard place to work. And I think that  I mean, I can even remember each time I'm out there it feels like my safety glasses are melting to my face, because it feels like you're working in an oven. It's very, very hot. But I think the key takeaway for me is that the resilience and the dedication of the 11,000 people that are out there working, trying to deliver this, I think the photos speak for themselves in terms of what's been accomplished so far.
 So we talked about  we've always talked about the initial evacuation methodology via trucking  that's really more than just trucking; it's an end-to-end logistics plan. I think the keys for our success there are fourfold.
 First of all, the detailed planning, and then how that is translated into safe operating procedures, and then the control measures that we have in place and contingency planning.
 I think we've put a lot of effort into that control and tracking. We've got vehicle tracking systems on all the vehicles. We've built three large transit centers along the route to make sure that we have place for the drivers to rest, recuperate, and as well as emergency response.
 So we're ready to go. We're going to start with small volumes and we're going to ramp up as safe and operationally efficient. We'll be able to give you a better guidance of what we're going to be able to achieve probably in October when we talk again.
 Shifting to the pipeline, I think we flagged for you all along that the monsoons were going to be a challenge. We're now fully in the monsoon period. But as most of you have been familiar with India, monsoons are a fact of life, and the keys to success are what planning and contingencies you put in place.
 Our contingencies have really all been about taking  working along this huge, long 600 kilometer pipeline at the monsoon periods, then focusing in all those resources into key areas that we need to deliver. So it's more of a rifle shot into what our challenges are and where we can work.
 So our focus really has been, if you look on the map, it's a sort of a schematic map, but our focus has really been  on mainline construction work, it's been in Rajasthan, where we have quite a lot more area where we're able to work during the monsoon period.
 Then in Gujarat, where we have a lot of the pipe already in the ground, all the effort has gone around into pre-commissioning and commissioning activities, mainly in the East.
 The West, because of soil conditions, and the very, very heavy rains there now, we're really not able to do a whole lot of work, because you can't move around the heavy equipment and personnel. So a lot of that work will remain 'til after the monsoons, and we'll move those resources there to try to progress the progress in that area.
 I think we've flagged for you a lot of factors in the impact on construction efficiency as we've gone throughout, but we're still very much working towards the target of Train 2 and pipeline by the end of the year.
 Just a couple of photos there for the scale of the project. I think when you look at the photo there, you're struck by how long it is, but that belies the tremendous amount of work that's going out on the field. There's a tremendous operation out there. We've got 5,000 people working on this, and it's interesting to step back and realize what we're doing. We're essentially building the world's longest heated pipeline. No one's done this before on this sort of scale, and we're doing it  we're building it in India, with Indian contractors and Indian stakeholders. So it's a tremendous achievement, and it's important to step back every now and then. And as I do that, I'm very proud of what the team has really accomplished so far.
 Just a couple of points to hit on crude sales. I think the guidance that we have given you guys all along has essentially been borne out. The price has really been a result of the chemistry of the oil, as we talked about. We've achieved a low sulfur benchmark as an agreement that's traded in the area. And, of course, that's adjusted for the price of the products. And that's been achieved within the production sharing contract mechanism that we've talked about all along.
 I think the uncertainties have always been around the just-in-time decision making that seems to result from working with so many varied stakeholders. But I think becoming operationally ready has then allowed us to facilitate the  removing most of the regulatory barriers and the price issues, so now we sit with a price agreed, as well as nominated volumes for the initial volumes.
 There is still future volumes that are yet to be agreed. Those future volumes you can expect  as you've lived through it now, you should expect a similar level of news flow and a similar level of uncertainty as a result of that. But I think the important thing is that we're on the same side of the table with the government of India. We're aligned in trying to maximize the long term value of the crude, and I think that ultimately will be borne out.
 So let me just conclude with one final slide and reiterate those four points.
 First of all, Train 1 is ready to go; you've seen some pictures. It's ready to start production by the end of the month.
 We have, I'd say, cautious confidence and growing optimism that we'll be able to complete the full project, Trains 2, Trains 3 and the pipeline in the first half of 2010.
 So we're essentially fixing the starting point, and we're telling you we're quite confident of the end point. However, there will be a lot of uncertainties on those individual milestones, and as we address the issues and uncertainties around commissioning each train and meeting the buyers' needs. So there will be uncertainty around the actual production ramp-up, but those things we manage on a daily basis.
 I think the third key takeaway is that getting operationally ready has led us to a point of being able to reduce the risk and uncertainty around oil price and the off-take volumes.
 And finally, the key point, I think, is that we've got an active evaluation program. We're excited about the future potential of the resource. We're putting actionable plans in place for the Barmer Hill, the EOR and the exploration and the discovered resources, the discovered fields, to try to answer the technical and operational questions that will allow us to get into full field development in those areas that provide us optionality for future growth, as well as starting to assess the exploration potential for the future.
 So that's all I had. I think we're taking questions at the end, so I'll turn it over to Dr. Watts.

Mike Watts,  Cairn Energy PLC - Deputy Chief Executive: Thank you, Rick. And good morning, everyone.
 I think that was a very lucid explanation from Rick on the focus and materiality that we've been about for the last few years. There is no more important project within Cairn than the delivery of the development in Mangala.
 As you know, everything we've done in Cairn has been home grown. Its exploration success has led to appraisal, development and then production success.
 The start of the process is exploration, and exploration is a pretty inexact science, particularly at the early stage of exploration. But I want to focus on where I think there is real future materiality for the Cairn Group. I want to pick up on some of the points that Rick has already made, and come back and start on Rajasthan. And I want to walk you through where we are in our understanding of Greenland which, as Bill said, is quite exciting.
 However, before I do, I just want to pick out a couple of other areas just for the sake of completion; one or two slides in the appendices relating to the Mediterranean.
 We only have one obligation well in this Company in the next year, and that's in Tunisia. We'll be drilling a well middle of next year in Tunisia. Everything else we do in the Company is discretionary, and in these uncertain financial times, the financial discipline that brings the Company, I think, is one of the strengths.
 We are also just about to shoot a 3D seismic survey in Albania. We completed, or Talisman, the operator, completed a 3D seismic in Papua New Guinea. Both Papua New Guinea and Albania are carbonate reef build-ups, and there's a slide showing you there's a pretty good close similarity between those two prospects. Albania's worth noting because of the superb commercial terms.
 Finally, Iraq; there is a slide on Iraq. There's really not much to say. We do have a seat at the table. In Istanbul today, the industry is with the Iraqi government as they go through the second round process. Bids will be in the end of this year and awards next year.
 But it's really they're looking  because these are all appraisal projects, they're looking for four years from now for field development plan submission. And, as we all know, the challenge is not so much technical, it's commercial.
 So if I just pick up on some of Rick's comments on Rajasthan and point to why this project is important to Cairn, and will remain important to Cairn for many years to come.
 Between '95 and '92, we made two discoveries; the Guda field and the Saraswati field. One is non-operator and one is operator. We managed to get a license extension from May 2002 to May 2005, and we went on to drill about 140 wells. In the period we coined the phrase, drill 'til you drop, and that was important, because it was the end of May 2005 which determined the size of the acreage position that we were able to retain under a long term contract.
 So that 140 wells presented us with a wall of information. We made discoveries in the Thumbli, the Dharvi Dungar, the Barmer Hill, but it was really the Fatehgarh discoveries in Mangala, Bhagyam and Aishwariya which transformed the Company. But that was a wall of data and it was difficult to remain on top of that information as it came in.
 And what's happening in Delhi right now is we are assembling a very, very experienced team of people to sift through all this data and actually, as Rick says, go on and look at new plays.
 But I'd like to stand back, and it is an inexact science. What has this basin actually generated in terms of hydrocarbon? And the guestimates, and they are guestimates, have a very wide range. It's probably somewhere between 25 and 50 billion barrels of oil, and we've got a good handle on about 10% of that that has been retained and captured, which is a pretty high, efficient entrapment rate.
 But if we look at the fields, the 22 that we've discovered, roughly the figure is somewhere 3.5, 3.7 billion barrels in place. And I'd like to just stick with in place numbers for the moment because it's an easy way of looking at apples and apples.
 That's a substantial in place resource and there's possibly more to find. This is an appraisal and development area, so it's difficult to talk about exploration, but the contingent resource is still quite significant.
 The work is ongoing, and over the coming months and years, we will still be reporting the volumes of this basin. But a reasonable target is certainly 5 billion barrels in place for the basin, and perhaps numbers even significantly higher than that.
 But the three Fatehgarh fields, Mangala, Bhagyam and Aishwariya, are together just over 2 billion barrels in place. That's where the focus is, and everything that Rick has been talking about is the Mangala field.
 Those three fields have world class reservoirs, porosities, permeabilities, reservoir thickness, reservoir extent. We are looking to retain  the target is as close to 50% recovery factors as possible, and even beyond may be possible in the future.
 Just as a comparison, the Mangala field then would  equates roughly to BP's Wytch Farm, which is the largest onshore field in the UK. And the three fields together would equate to the volumes of Schoonebeek, which is Shell's largest onshore field  industry's largest onshore field in Europe. So significant volumes.
 But the interesting point Rick has mentioned. There's about 1 billion barrels in the mixed bag that's essentially Barmer Hill, but other fields. Swings and roundabouts; the review is ongoing, and some fields get poorer, some fields get better.
 When we reported on these a few years ago, the target was a 2% to 5% recovery factor. There are indications, and it's only indications, the work's not complete. Some of these fields may be able to achieve 10%, or perhaps even 15% or 20%.
 So the target for the Company is, what can we extract in the future from these fields? The infrastructure, the pipeline that we're talking about, is all carried and justified through Mangala.
 The other fields, the exploration, or the exploration potential, who knows what the recovery factor ? At an un-risked basis, it could be 1 or 2 billion barrels in place. However, on a risked basis it could be zero. It's just there is a lot of scope for growth, and the infrastructure that we're putting in will allow for that growth. So it remains a very exciting project for Cairn.
 The other material project we want to talk about is Greenland. I'll start off with a map of the whole North Atlantic. If you look at the North Atlantic province, there's exploration success and production right across both the North American side and the European side; a tremendous amount of activity over the last 40 years. There's been very little activity in Greenland; six wells drilled on the West Coast, five of which were drilled in the '70s. No wells in the North, South or East.

I think overall the pricing environment is pretty stable.
 There is a lot of customer sensitivity, and Ed said it very well in his comments. I think large companies continue to understand that you have got to find that threshold or you have got to find that market dynamic. What is the market willing to pay?

Robin Lampard,  Norbord Inc. - SVP and CFO: Thanks, Barrie. I'll begin with a few comments regarding markets. The US housing market remains challenging. Year-to-date housing starts, including multi-family, are approximately 2% lower than last year. Single-family starts, which are more important to the OSB industry, are down 12% versus last year. Nonetheless, North American OSB prices did hold up during the third quarter.
 The North Central benchmark OSB price improved somewhat to $184 per thousand square feet compared to $173 in the prior quarter and $180 during the same quarter last year. In the Southeast region, where approximately 55% of Norbord's North American capacity is located, the price averaged $169 in Q3 versus $162 in Q2 and $156 in Q3 of last year.
 In Europe, overall panel demand softened slightly due to slowing construction and retail spending. Panel prices, however, continued to trend up compared to both the prior quarter and the same quarter last year, reflecting the ongoing increases we are facing on wood, resin and energy costs.
 Quarter-over-quarter, particleboard and MDF prices increased by 7% and 3%, respectively, while OSB prices eased 2%. Year-over-year, average particleboard, MDF, and OSB prices increased by 20%, 16% and 6%, respectively, in order to recover input cost escalation.
 And now, to our results. As Barrie mentioned, we generated positive EBITDA of $12 million in the third quarter. This compares to $10 million in the second quarter and $13 million in the third quarter of last year. Norbord recorded a loss of $1 million or $0.02 per share in the third quarter compared to earnings of $1 million or $0.03 per share in the second quarter and a loss of $4 million or $0.09 per share in the third quarter of 2010.
 I'll point out that our income tax recovery this quarter is quite a bit higher than you might have expected due to the fact that we operate in multiple jurisdictions with different tax rates, and currency rates were particularly volatile this quarter.
 Our North American operations generated EBITDA of $5 million this quarter versus breakeven in the prior quarter and $4 million in the same quarter last year. Year-over-year, higher productivity and lower key input usages more than offset higher resin and fiber prices, and lower OSB mill nets. Quarter-over-quarter, higher OSB prices and lower resin and fiber usages more than offset higher energy and fiber prices. Q3 OSB shipment volumes were 4% higher than the prior quarter and in line with the same quarter last year.
 Norbord's operating North American OSB mills continued to run at approximately 85% of capacity this quarter. Including the two indefinitely closed mills in Huguley, Alabama and Jefferson, Texas, our operations ran at about 65% of capacity in both the third and second quarters of 2011, slightly lower than the 70% in the third quarter of 2010. Despite running 5% more curtailed, we've been able to hold our production volumes steady versus last year, thanks to the significant productivity improvements we've achieved.
 Our North American OSB cash production cost per unit decreased by 1% versus both the prior quarter and the same quarter last year. Excluding the impact of higher raw material prices, our controllable unit cost decreased even more, by 2% quarter-over-quarter and 4% year-over-year. This is the result of the improved manufacturing productivity I just mentioned and lower raw materials usage.
 Our European operations continued to run at full capacities, generating EBITDA of $10 million this quarter versus $13 million in the prior quarter and $11 million in the same quarter last year. Year-over-year, higher panel prices and shipment volumes were offset by higher prices for all key raw material inputs. Quarter-over-quarter, lower shipment volumes and higher resin costs were only partially offset by higher panel prices. Q3 panel shipment volume was 6% lower than Q2, but 6% higher than Q3 last year and is up about 15% year-to-date.
 Our European operations have generated EBITDA of $34 million year-to-date versus $25 million in 2010, a $9 million increase. Higher shipment volumes and lower raw materials usages delivered these improvements, while higher selling prices offset the impact of higher costs for all key inputs.
 Focusing on our margin improvement program for a moment, MIP benefits continued to accelerate and we've generated $21 million in gains year-to-date. These benefits come from a richer sales mix, improved production efficiencies, and reduced raw materials usage and particularly in North America, have helped offset the negative impact of higher raw material prices. MIP represents our single-most-important operating focus in these challenging markets and we are on track to deliver our full-year target of $30 million in improvements.
 Turning now to our balance sheet and cash flow, operating working capital was $65 million at period-end compared to $52 million in the prior quarter and $49 million in the prior year. The quarter-over-quarter increase was primarily due to the timing of sales and collections of accounts receivable. And the year-over-year increase was due to higher accounts receivable and inventory.
 Receivables were higher due to higher prices and sales volume in Europe and the timing of sales and collections. Inventories were higher due to more finished goods in transit over quarter-end. So the increase in both these periods is really just timing. Working capital remains well controlled and accounts receivable performance is in line with prior periods.
 CapEx totaled $4 million this quarter and $16 million year-to-date. Our CapEx target for the year is $25 million. This is modestly higher than last year, due to the completion of the Cowie, Scotland particleboard mill upgrades we talked about last quarter.
 You will have seen in our Q3 disclosure documents referenced to our plans for our upcoming July 2012 bond maturity. I told you last quarter that this debt maturity has been on our radar for some time, but that we didn't want to refinance it too early given the significant make-whole we would have had to pay on an early call of the bonds.
 It is still our intention to refinance the bonds prior to their July 1 maturity, but recognizing the current volatile state of financial markets and to provide additional flexibility in case it is needed, we've now put in place a backup refinancing plan. If required, we have the option to repay up to half of this $240 million maturity from our bank lines and the other half from $120 million lending commitment from our largest shareholder, Brookfield.
 In addition, we amended our committed revolving bank lines, so that the net debt to total capitalization covenant is now 65% instead of 60%. This backup plan and the bank amendments provide the flexibility and liquidity Norbord needs to manage through these volatile financial markets and what appears to be an extended housing recovery.
 We finished the quarter with $55 million in cash and $262 million in undrawn revolving bank lines. This is in addition to the $120 million Brookfield commitment I just outlined. Rachel Lavine,  Gazit-Globe, Ltd. - CEO: Thank you, Sarah, and good day to you all. Firstly, I would like to thank you for joining us on this conference call to review the results of the second quarter for the year 2016. Today, I will briefly discuss our activities in the markets in which we operate, together with some of the main highlights of events within the Group. I will touch upon the financial results for the quarter and our CFO, Adi Jemini, will then address the financial results in greater detail later on.
 During this quarter, we have continued to improve the quality of our portfolio, a process whose objective is to increase the cash flows while reinforcing our competitive position in our various markets of operation. In the three months' period ending June 2016, we have invested approximately ILS1.1 billion in acquisition, development, and redevelopment of our assets. Additionally, we have disposed of noncore assets in the aggregate amount of approximately ILS430 million. I will refer to some examples later on during this call.
 At the end of the quarter, our balance sheet includes assets valued at ILS3.7 billion which are under development or redevelopment, with a total cost to complete of approximately ILS2 billion. These properties, which are located in leading cities like Toronto, San Francisco, Sao Paulo, Helsinki, and Warsaw, will contribute to our revenue in the coming quarters and in particular during the course of 2017.
 Our balance sheet shows a reduction in LTV levels both on a consolidated basis and on a solo basis. Additionally, shareholder equity increased significantly by ILS0.5 billion for a total of ILS7.9 billion. This increase is attributed mainly to: a substantial increase in the value of the investment properties by the amount of approximately ILS570 million during the quarter; the FFO for the quarter; and to the impact of foreign exchange rate; although this increase was partly offset by dividend distribution and by the devaluation of financial instruments.
 Since the beginning of the year, we have increased and diversified our lines of credit from banking institutions while at the same time reducing the cost of credit, with the result that our financing costs decreased by approximately 20 basis points. Furthermore, S&P Maalot has recently reaffirmed the Company local debt rating ilAA- with stable outlook.
 Alongside the increase in revenue and NOI during this quarter, we also report a decrease in FFO and FFO per share in comparison to the same quarter of 2015. The decrease in FFO is due principally to the strengthening of the shekel, the revaluation of financial derivatives, and the partial sale of shares in FCR and Equity One. The equity share issuance which was completed at the end of 2015, has also resulted in a reduction in the level of FFO per share.
 Turning now to review the operational results in the various territories in which we operate, in the US we continue to witness strong and very positive trends which find expression, among other things, in a very strong growth in the same-property NOI of 5% together with a significant increase of 7% in lease renewals for the quarter. Occupancy rates at the end of the quarter continued to rise to a level of 96.3%.
 Our US subsidiary has properties under development and redevelopment totaling $0.25 billion including Serramonte, which one of the best assets to be found in the West Coast. This asset is located in the entrance to San Francisco and it is being developed gradually with a cost to complete of approximately $90 million.
 Equity One is also working on the implementation of a development pipeline valued at several hundred million dollars over the course of the next few years, principally targeting leading urban properties located in areas with great potential for value accretion. As a result, our US subsidiary anticipates consistent and steady growth in NOI in the coming years.
 The target cash on cost yields are between 7% to 8% on current development. Equity One also shows a very strong financial position with an LTV of approximately 22.3%.
 In Canada, FCR continues to show good growth figures, with occupancy rates rising almost 50 basis points over the corresponding period last year to a level of 95.2% as well as a 5.9% increase in lease renewals. In addition, FCR reports same-property NOI, which excluding a nonrecurring item during the corresponding quarter, totaled approximately 1.6%.
 During the second quarter, FCR carried out investment totaling approximately CAD117 million. Following their reporting period, FCR announced it has entered into a binding agreement for the acquisition of a prime super-urban property located at the intersection of Yonge and Bloor Street in the heart of downtown Toronto in consideration for approximately CAD190 million.
 This location, which is one of the busiest intersections in Canada, is similar in character to Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, New York. The property includes the direct connection to the subway station through which in excess of 400,000 passengers commute on a daily basis. This acquired property consists of three floors of retail space measuring approximately 7,900 square meters.
 The asset is located within five minutes walk from Yorkville, where FCR already has a strong position, so that this acquisition is expected to dramatically enhance our footprint in the region. This property is another example of our ongoing strategy in recent years to focus on leading urban areas and to significantly improve the quality of our portfolio.
 At the same time, during the past two weeks, FCR has completed an equity issuance of approximately CAD173 million at a price of CAD22.60 per share, the proceeds of which are to be attributed in part to the financing of the acquisition just mentioned.
 In Northern Europe, the acquisition of the Norwegian assets of Sektor have contributed for the most part to the increase of approximately 34% in NOI. The occupancy rates remained stable at 96.5%. Regarding the same-property NOI, if we include a material asset which is jointly controlled, Kista, as well as the Norwegian portfolio, we will show an increase of 0.9%.
 In the coming year and more especially during 2017, we expect to see an increase in NOI in Northern Europe resulting from the completion of development and redevelopment projects. The growth in NOI will be generated principally by the extension of our flagship asset in Helsinki, Iso Omena, which is partly open this month and which is expected to be completed during the first half of 2017.
 In addition, since the beginning of this year Citycon has completed the sale of noncore assets in the aggregate amount of approximately EUR98 million as part of an ongoing process to further improve the quality of our portfolio in the region.
 In Central and Eastern Europe, we report a decline in NOI and same-property NOI. But if we exclude Russia, the revenue in our core markets in Poland, the Czech Republic, and Slovakia showed an increase of 1% while net income from the same-property NOI in these countries increased by 0.5%. Since the beginning of this year, we have purchased Atrium's share in an aggregate amount of approximately EUR30 million.
 In Brazil, we continue to identify encouraging economic indicators such as the sharp rise in share price since the beginning of the year, which signals an expectation of positive change in the economic environment. In addition, the yield on 10-year bond, which stood over 16% in January, now stands at 11.8%. The fall in yields support the rise in real estate values and the prices of income-producing assets, which is indicative of growing confidence in the country's economy.
 We have recently announced the disposal of shares held in BR Malls to a shareholding of less than 5%, while at the same time increasing our direct ownership in real estate by investing approximately $47 million in the Top Center Complex in Sao Paulo. This acquisition will allow us to increase the GLA while creating value to an urban and very strategic asset. To date, our investment in BR Malls represents a realized and as-yet-unrealized profit totaling over ILS130 million.
 Following the reporting date, we opened the first stage of Morumbi shopping center in Sao Paulo. This asset is comprised of approximately 30,000 square meters and is occupied by two leading anchor tenants, namely Tok&Stok, household food retail chain, and Zaffari, which is one of the leading and best-quality supermarket chains in Brazil. The property is located in the main street of a city district with high socioeconomic demographics.
 The Israeli portfolio is stable and we're presently in the final stage of completing the transaction to increase our shareholding in Gazit Israel to 100%. This transaction is compatible with our declared business strategy of increasing our ownership of private real estate and of simplifying the structure of the Company.
 On the morning of September 27, we will conduct an investor conference at the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange with the participation of the CEOs of both North American subsidiaries, Equity One and First Capital, during which we will give a review of our operation in that region. This presents a golden opportunity not only to gain more detailed and focused exposure to our activities in North America but also to learn about the latest developments in the US and the Canadian markets, which have been our core markets of activities in the past 20 years and which continue to be included among the most stable, growing markets in the world. We will send an invitation to this event within the next few days.
 With that, I would like to turn the call over to Adi Jemini for in-depth review of our financial results. Adi, please.

Adi Jemini,  Gazit-Globe, Ltd. - CFO: Thank you, Rachel. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. I'll spend a few minutes putting our results into context and then make some comments to our balance sheet.
 Starting on slide 4, the operational results for the quarter were solid throughout our core markets with a 3% increase in NOI, or 5.4% if we cover the FX impact. The strength of our result is also shown through our improvement of our NOI margin by 1.6%, or to 71%.
 To better understand the operating results, I will break down the NOI by regions, each based on its original currency. As expected, a significant increase of 33.9% in Northern Europe, which is mainly due to the acquisition of the Norwegian portfolio. An increase of 5% in the US, driven by unprecedented high tenant demand reflected through our solid leasing spread, whereas Canada showed a positive trend with a strong and stable NOI the quarter.
 A decrease of 6% in Central and Eastern Europe, which is driven from the decrease in Russia of approximately 11%, while in our core markets such as Poland, we've seen stable and positive trends.
 In terms of our private platform results, in Brazil our NOI increased by 25%, mostly due to the acquisition of high-quality urban properties in Sao Paulo City. In Israel, our NOI remained stable.
 With respect to cash flows, we see a substantial increase of ILS572 million in fair value of real estate, which was the main factor for our net income of ILS97 million. It is noteworthy to mention this profit does not include the plus ILS105 million unrealized gain in BR Malls which is recorded in the OCI.
 Moving on to slide 5, a few comments on our first half-year results. For the six months year-to-date, we see a similar trend in operational results, with an increase of about 2.7% in NOI, or 7% if we exclude the FX impact. Like the quarterly results, the drivers for the increase are due to our strong operating fundamentals in North America as a result of healthy leasing spreads and redevelopment, coupled with significant increase in North Europe due to the Norwegian acquisition, offset by a decrease in Central and Eastern Europe, and particularly due to the decrease of 17% in NOI in Russia.
 The strength of our underlying real estate assets is also reflected through a significant increase in cash flows from operating activities of more than 20%, alongside a substantial increase in fair value of ILS821 million. The overall positive trends in Q2, which resulted in ILS97 million in net income for the Q2, is being offset by the Q1 net loss of ILS278 million which was mainly due to the ILS230 million loss related to Dori Group.
 Slide 6. This slide illustrates our operational results for the quarter. As you can see, excluding the FX impact the rental income and NOI increased by 3% and 5.4%, respectively, while FFO and FFO per share decreased by 8% and 6%, respectively.
 It's worth spending a moment on FFO and understanding the movement. The decrease in FFO per share was mainly due to the following: foreign currency effects; the sale of shares of Equity One and FCR, including prior-year disposition of our noncore medical office segment in the United States. The additional decrease of FFO per share compared to the total FFO is due to the equity issuance at the end of fiscal-year 2015.
 If we further feel the FX by currency, you'll know that most of the impact came from the 6.1% decline in the Canadian dollars. And despite a sharper decrease of 12.6% of the Brazilian reais, its impact was much of a lesser extent.
 Moving on to slide 7, our portfolio in the US continued to perform very well with a robust same-store NOI growth of 5%, or 5.5% including redevelopment. The growth is driven by a strong tenant demand as evidenced by a healthy leasing spread of approximately 7% and increase of occupancy of 90 basis points compared with prior year.
 In Canada, same-store NOI was impacted by two significant lease termination fees that were received in Q2 2015, which totaled about CAD3 million. Excluding these fees, same-store NOI grew by 1.6% for the six months of fiscal-year 2016. Similar with the US, we continue to see a healthy lift on our leasing renewals of 7%, an increase of occupancy of 50 basis points, reaching 95.2% occupancy rates at the end of the period.
 The strong results in North America also translated into overall average rental rate growth of 1.8% and 7.4% in Canada and USA, respectively, compared with prior year of 2015.
 As I mentioned in our previous call, it's important to note that in Northern Europe same-store NOI excludes the following: one, the recent acquisition of Sektor, which represents 30% of our Northern Europe value, which showed a 3% same-store NOI growth; two, Kista Galleria, one of our strongest and most valuable assets in Stockholm, which showed a 3.8% NOI growth; and, three, our flagship asset in Helsinki, Iso Omena, which is undergoing a 30,000 square-meter redevelopment in the tune of EUR250 million and is expected to open during fiscal-year 2017.
 In Central and Eastern Europe, we see a decrease of 3.9%; and, as expected, that decrease is driven by 20% same-store NOI decrease in Russia. Excluding Russia, we show an increase of 0.9%.
 We also see positive trends in most markets. Together with the US that enjoyed a very positive trend, Sweden shows an increase of 4.5% in same-store NOI, and the Czech Republic showed an increase of about 3.1%, and Slovakia 1.6%. Despite Russia, the overall result is a product of our strong real estate and a testament to our quality of urban portfolio across the globe.
 Lastly, consolidated occupancy increased by 30 basis points and continued to be strong at 95.7%.
 Continuing on page 8, the increase in the fair value of investment property during the quarter was high and totaled ILS572 million. We continue to see positive trends in the valuation of assets, driven by cap rates compression in most of our core urban markets.
 The cap rates in our core assets market in the US, Canada, and Northern Europe was around 5.5%. It is noteworthy to mention that the growth in Europe was mainly due to the revaluation of assets in Norway and Sweden.
 In Brazil, we saw a decrease of ILS24 million mainly due to the increase of 30 basis points in the cap rate. We focus our investments activities primarily in the development and redevelopment that represent about 53% of the total investment or more than ILS2 billion this year. And this activity of redevelopment will be the fuel that will generate additional growth in the upcoming years.
 Turning to our balance sheet on slide 9, shareholders' equity totaled ILS7.9 billion, representing an increase of approximately ILS0.5 billion during the quarter or ILS2.5 per share. Compared with year-end, our shareholders' equity increased by ILS355 million or ILS1.8 per share. The increase is primarily due to the fair value gain for the period, foreign currency impact, and FFO; which offset by a ILS195 million loss in Q1 as a result of the Dori Group deconsolidation.
 As we indicated, we continue to focus on deleveraging, and we show a continuous improvement of our LTV both on a consolidated level and on our standalone. As of June 30, our consolidated LTV is at 50.8%, a decrease of 50 basis points compared with December 31, 2015. On a standalone basis, our market LTV decreased significantly by 5.5% to 57.6%, compared with 63% in Q2 of 2015.
 Moving on to slide 10, we have a strong balance sheet with a high liquidity of approximately ILS9.8 billion on a consolidated basis, of which ILS2.3 billion is at the Company level. As I mentioned in the previous call, on the parent level we continue to work towards maintaining a high level of liquidity while diversifying the sources of the Company both in Israel and abroad.
 Capital raising in the Group level totaled about ILS1.4 billion, with the vast majority of it was in North America. Our unencumbered pool of assets grew over the quarter to ILS62.3 billion; or simply put, 80% of our assets are free and clear as of June 30, 2016.
 Subsequent to quarter-end, S&P Maalot reconfirmed our local rating at AA- level with a stable outlook. The high credit rating of Gazit confirms the Group's financial strength, and we are committed to continuing working towards further improving our financial ratios as we seek to attain international credit rating down the road.
 Continuing on slide 11, we have a well staggered maturity profile, with approximately 8% of our debt coming due in the year. The headline here is that by the end of fiscal-year 2016 we will have paid about ILS1 billion of debt and we have no plans to issue bonds in the domestic market in the coming months.
 This concludes my comments on the financial results. I'd like to hand the call over for questions. Operator?
================================================================================

Allow me to give you some figures. At times, we had 16,000 employees working from home. So far, we have distributed more than 190 masks to members of our workforce, sent 220,000 rapid tests to people and started to vaccinate staff at our Hanau site. Our aim is to vaccinate all our employees and their families as quickly as possible. At present, we are waiting for sufficient amounts of vaccine and the necessary permits.
 Logistics and supply chains were most important in the crisis. And here, we were also able to respond in a robust manner. Thanks to our global network of reliable partners, we coped well with the challenges, and were able to maintain production and deliveries throughout the world.
 Ladies and gentlemen, we are aware of our special social responsibility, especially during periods of crisis. We rapidly increased production capacities for disinfectants to meet rising demand. And we supported and supplied institutions in communities close to our sites and supplied them with these materials. Together with our customers, we donated our high-performance polymer PA12 for the manufacturer of protective medical equipment. And recently, we reported that we are driving forward production of vaccines against COVID-19 by setting up the production and supply of special lipids exceptionally fast. What would normally take at least a year or rather much longer has been achieved in less than 6 months.
 We received the first request from vaccine producer BioNTech in Mainz in November 2020. To transport its novel mRNA vaccine safely to cells in the human body the long-chained molecules are encapsulated in a lipid particle. As well as protecting the sensitive mRNA, this custom-tailored shell helps transport it to the cells. BioNTech awarded us a contract to produce these essential lipids. In response, production at our sites in Hanau and Dossenheim was ramped up in record time, with the support in the form of precursors and knowledge coming from the entire Evonik Group, from Marl to Mapleton. This is our modest contribution, effective contribution to combating this pandemic.
 Ladies and gentlemen, our financial performance and the ongoing strategic development of the group also go to show that Evonik proved resilient in the crisis. Above all, they are ample proof that we once again walked the talk and delivered what we promised, despite the extreme situation. We were one of the few companies that had the courage to issue earnings guidance in May 2020, shortly after the outbreak of the crisis. And we achieved that forecast almost exactly to the euro during the year. In fact, our free cash flow was even exceeded.
 Adjusted earnings before financial result, taxes, depreciation and amortization came in at EUR 1.9 billion, exactly in the middle of the range we forecast in May 2020. Sales were EUR 12.2 billion, around 7% lower than in the previous year. However, that was a respectable result in the context of the most serious economic crisis since the Second World War. Our free cash flow was really good at EUR 780 million. It was well above the prior year level. Our adjusted net income was, therefore, EUR 640 million giving adjusted earnings per share of EUR 1.37. Achieving our goals was only possible thanks to improved quality and the resulting increase in the robustness of our portfolio, which we have steadily restructured in recent years.
 Our 3 growth divisions, which are at the heart of our portfolio, generated 95% of earnings from our operating business in 2020. I presented our new divisional structure to you last year already. Despite the difficult situation, it was launched on schedule during the year. The former operating chemicals segments have been transferred to 4 divisions, which are more balanced in terms of size and type of business. Moreover, they can be managed better, thanks to clear strategic roles, shared end markets and a clear allocation to technology platforms. The Specialty Additives, Nutrition & Care and Smart Materials divisions are clearly aligned to growth. Performance Materials is particularly lean and efficient.
 We are reaping the benefits of this accomplishment, and this is reflected also in our financial figures. As already mentioned, our adjusted EBITDA was EUR 1.9 billion, that was a decline of 11% at group level. However, earnings from our 3 growth divisions, Specialty Additives, Nutrition & Care and Smart Materials, were only 3% lower. The growth and resilience of these 3 new divisions are actually driven by two factors  by 2 elements  key elements. First, the high proportion of environment-friendly and sustainable solutions. Second, our innovative capability, and that's our innovative new products and innovative solutions. These 2 elements make us stand out clearly in the market and in what we offer to our customers.
 Allow me to present some examples from our 3 growth divisions. Specialty Additives brings together our broad spectrum of Specialty Additives. Sometimes it's difficult to speak and I have a dry throat when I talk about our impressive divisions. Specialty Additives brings together our broad spectrum of Specialty Additives, which enhance the quality of our customers' products, save energy and quite simply, in many respects, make them better. An impressive example is the self-adhesive labels without a backing material that we developed at Evonik. Normally, self adhesive labels generate a great deal of waste because they require a release liner until they are actually applied. Evonik's technology prevents such waste being generated in the first place, because our silicones eliminate the need for an additional liner. As well as reducing the total weight by 40% and cutting down the related material costs, that saves resources as well.
 The Nutrition & Care division is focused on people's well-being. In other words, their health and quality of life. Earlier on, I already mentioned that we had set up production of lipids for BioNTech in record time. That is probably the best example of innovation and speed. Another project focused on sustainable innovation that is very close to our heart, actually, is the development of biosurfactants that are 100% biodegradable. The first industrial-scale production facility for these products, scheduled for 2023, will be a real milestone. We have already received initial recognition for this. Our partner, Unilever, has opted for the collaboration with Evonik as a key element in its Clean Future initiative to drive forward the decarbonization of its products.
 The Smart Materials division pools our business with innovative materials that enable resource-saving solutions and replace conventional materials. We are the global leader in PA12 powders for 3D printing. Just recently, we launched a new generation of powders for 3D printing. About 80% of the product can be recycled in the printing process, making a strong contribution to tomorrow's circular economy. Another perfect and nice example, maybe really perfect example of innovation driven by sustainability, is a new anode material for lithium-ion batteries. We recently launched this product under the trade name Siridion Black. It improves the performance of batteries by increasing their energy density and improving their fast-charging capability and energy efficiency.
 As you can no doubt imagine, I could easily talk for far longer about Evonik's impressive projects. However, I also want to look at the progress with our strategy, without which these successes I've just highlighted would not have been possible. These innovations would have been inconceivable without this progress of our strategy.
 Ladies and gentlemen, although we are still a long way from our goal, we have made considerable progress in implementing our strategy in recent years. We continued this process in 2020 despite all the hindrances that surrounded us during this period of time. 4 years ago, that was back in 2017, we embarked on a transformation process at Evonik. If you think of this process as a 100-meter sprint, we are currently about halfway. We've achieved a number of successes over the past 4 years, and we intend to do a lot in the future. And this involves great potential.
 Let us first look at corporate culture. We've established a strong culture that rewards above-average performance, supports diversity, encourages innovation and focuses on sustainability. We've also taken the next steps in a systematic integration of sustainability into our business strategy. I'm convinced that in the long term, only those companies that operate responsibly and create value for society will be successful. We are committed to this principle, and we are convinced of the correctness of this principle. And we are guided by this principle.
 Against this backdrop, ladies and gentlemen, we have been able to achieve a major milestone. Over the past few years, we've conducted the first sustainability analysis of all our businesses. To put it in a nutshell, every product line has been examined to establish what value it creates for society and the environment, and its footprint; in other words, the emissions released during production. In 2020, we completed this evaluation of our entire chemicals portfolio. A particularly positive finding of this analysis is that around 35% of our products already offer higher sustainability benefit than comparable competing products. Given this quality and given this superiority, these products show highly attractive growth rates. We call this group of products next generation solutions.
 Our ambitious goal is to steadily increase the proportion of this product category in the coming years, naturally with the help of our research and development. From our corporate purpose, leading beyond chemistry to improve life today and tomorrow, we derive the aspiration of being a global leader with our innovations on a global basis. With that in mind, we have restructured our organization and pooled our capabilities to bring our scientific expertise even closer to our markets and customers, and to speed up the development of new solutions and applications.
 We aim to generate additional sales of EUR 1 billion by 2025 with innovations from our 6 innovation growth fields. Here, we virtually started from scratch, from 0 virtually in 2015 and had already generated additional sales of EUR 350 million by the end of 2020. Turning to portfolio management. In the past 4 years, we have divested cyclical businesses with sales of EUR 2 billion. In the same period, we've strengthened our portfolio by adding higher value and less cyclical specialty businesses of similar size. All the disposals, all the divestments were made at attractive prices in favorable phases of the economic cycle.
 Rest assured that we will be continuing this policy. Since the fall of 2020, we have therefore been preparing to carve out the Baby Care business to pave the way for a realignment of these operations with a partner or new owner. The acquisitions have strengthened the growth and the resilience of our business, reduced our overall capital intensity and have so far leveraged cumulative annual synergies of EUR 70 million. In 2020, we continued to make rapid progress with the integration of our most recent investments. That included both the successful closing of the acquisition of the U.S. company, PeroxyChem, and the acquisition of catalyst specialist Porocel, which we successfully completed at the end of the year.
 At present, we are also driving growth through our largest investment in Germany. More than EUR 400 million have been invested in the PA12 complex at our largest site, Marl Chemical Park in North Rhine-Westphalia. This complex will come onstream in 2021. The investment is a perfect fit, actually, with our strategy of systematically focusing on specialty chemicals, because polyamide 12 is a high-performance polymer that is used in many demanding applications. For example, it is used as a substitute for steel in automotive engineering and lightweight structures, and for special solutions for medical technology and 3D-printing. Therefore it is an important and essential part of our Smart Materials growth engine.
 We are also focusing on growth and efficiency when it comes to the business with amino acids. Specifically, that means that in the future, Evonik will be concentrating its methionine production at 3 state-of-the-art sites in Asia, Europe and in the United States. At the end of March 2021, we closed our oldest and smallest production facility in Germany. That will generate economies of scale, cost savings and will, therefore, also strengthen our global cost leadership. And while we are on the subject of costs. In the past, cost discipline, well, was not one of our strengths. That is another thing that has changed, as 2020 proves. Cost discipline is firmly established and is now a firm part of our corporate DNA and is part of the self-perception of this group. We successfully completed our SG&A program last year. You will definitely remember that in 2018, we announced planned savings of EUR 200 million.
 And here again, we've kept our promise. If you look at our income statement today, you will see that we actually achieved more, that we actually exceeded our target with savings of EUR 230 million. We keep a close eye on cost trends in both our operating business and our administrative operations. We refer to this as ApEx and OpEx. ApEx means that we will be pursuing the continuous improvement of our administrative structures even after the completion of our SG&A program. If you will, we could say that this is the final touch in our profitable future growth alongside our growth divisions, which are driven by innovation and sustainability.
 Dear shareholders, of course we want to make sure that you, our shareholders, also benefit from Evonik's successful performance. Based on our stable results in 2020, the Executive and Supervisory Board are, therefore, proposing a stable and attractive dividend of EUR 1.15 per share. We focus on dividend continuity at a high level, even or rather precisely in challenging times when earnings are declining. That is one of our highest priorities. Based on the closing share price at year-end 2020, that represents and is equivalent to a dividend yield of 4.3%. Ladies and gentlemen, dear shareholders, this is further evidence once again that Evonik shares are very attractive.
 Let us now take a look at the current fiscal year, namely 2021. The pandemic will continue to influence the economy this year. We will, therefore, still have to live with a certain amount of uncertainty. However, our robust performance over the past year and our confidence in our strengths mean that we can look ahead with great confidence. Since the end of last year, we have noticed a clear recovery, and we also made a strong start to the year. The global economy should grow by at least 4% this year. We expect Evonik to grow slightly faster.
 Based on our first quarter results, on May 6 we announced that we are not simply confirming our guidance, we are now more optimistic. We now expect adjusted EBITDA to be between EUR 2.1 billion and EUR 2.3 billion for the year as a whole. The signs are clearly pointing to growth. In 2021 already, we aim to exceed the pre pandemic performance reported in 2019. In the first quarter, sales grew 4% year-on-year to EUR 3.36 billion. Adjusted EBITDA compared with the year before was 15% higher at EUR 588 million. That was actually 9% more than in the first quarter of 2019. Our growth strategy is, therefore, successful. And again, our 3 growth divisions, Specialty Additives, Nutrition & Care and Smart Materials remain our drivers and are making an above-average contribution to this good performance. The free cash flow tripled to almost EUR 312 million in the first quarter, boosted by our improved business situation, the strict management of net working capital and lower taxes. This good start to the year makes us optimistic about this year, about 2021 and the future.
 Ladies and gentlemen, if we look at the stock market in 2020, we see that it was largely influenced by the impact of the coronavirus pandemic. Evonik shares started the year at around EUR 27 and reached their highest point very early on, at EUR 27.33 on January 2. The market went through many volatile phases during the year, mainly due to the global economic crisis and the virus-related information around the coronavirus. Our shares ended 2020 at EUR 26.38, which is a slight loss of around 2% over the year as a whole. Since the start of 2021, our share price performance has been far more pleasing. Fueled by more positive market sentiment and our more optimistic outlook, Evonik shares topped the EUR 30 mark with a year-to-date high of EUR 30.70 on April 6, 2021. In mid-May, on the 25th of May, the share price was EUR 29.27, which is equivalent to a rise of 9% since the beginning of the year. Evonik, therefore, outperformed the index, which rose by 6%. To enable our employees to participate in the increase in Evonik's value, a further tranche of our employee share program was launched in the Spring for employees in Germany, the United States, Belgium and Singapore. Worldwide, around 11,000 employees acquired shares in Evonik, which is equivalent to a take-up rate of nearly 41%.
 For this year's share program for employees, we purchased a total of 503,491 shares at an average price of EUR 29.75 and a theoretical share of the capital stock of EUR 1 per share. That was about 0.1% of our capital stock of EUR 466 million. For this, we used the authorization to purchase treasury stock granted at the Annual Shareholders' Meeting in 2020. All the shares have now been transferred to the eligible employees, and the surplus that was left has actually been sold on the market in the meantime.
 Ladies and gentlemen, as you have seen and heard, we have made very good progress in implementing our strategic agenda for the future. And as I have explained to you, there are further fascinating and interesting challenges ahead. Evonik's clear objective for the coming years is to continue its transformation into a specialty chemicals company with 100% growth businesses. That's not going to happen overnight, of course, but the direction is clearly defined. We will be continuing to actively manage our portfolio to make it more robust and increase the return on capital and cash generation.
 Our innovation and sustainability targets play a very important role in this transformation, along with further focused investment in growth, acquisitions, as well as the restructuring and divestment and disposal of the businesses.
 Thanks to my reappointment, I'm looking forward to continuing to shape and lead this strategic development with my colleagues on the Executive Board, our executives and our entire workforce. I would like to take this opportunity to thank the Supervisory Board, you, our shareholders, and of course, all Evonik employees for  and also our partners in industry and among the employees for your continued trust and support. I hope that you, our esteemed shareholders, will continue to place your confidence in Evonik in the future. And would like to thank you all on behalf of myself and my colleagues on the Executive Board for your interest and kind attention.
 Thank you. Please stay safe and take care.

 I'm pleased to report that we believe the technical issues have now been resolved and that customers are effectively processing the direct connect material. Consequently, we've been able to ramp up our production volumes in Paulinia, and we are now at approximately 90% of our planned production capacity. We continue to expect the direct connect state-of-the-art technology will enable efficient capacity expansions for our Cariflex business moving forward.
 We've also recently completed our USBC expansion in Berre, France, which was part of the overall $70 million of cost improvement initiatives for our Polymer segment that we announced back in June of 2015. We now look forward to leveraging the improved cost base and economics that we expect the expansion will provide.
 Overall market conditions in our paving and roofing markets remain relatively robust, as we move from an excellent summer season in South America, where our HiMA technology offerings enjoyed a 50% growth in sales volume as compared to the first quarter of last year, and through the traditional summer seasons of both North America and Europe. Thus, the timing of our Berre's expansion and its successful startup is well timed to take advantage of the paving season.
 Turning to our Chemical segment. First quarter 2018 adjusted EBITDA was $44 million, up 31% compared to the first quarter of 2017 with an associated margin of 20.8% (sic) [20.6%].  Looking ahead, after 2 years of delivering impressive cost reductions associated with both acquisition synergy initiatives and operational improvements, we expect 2018 to be a year of margin recovery versus the cycle lows that we experienced in 2017.
 Debt reduction, as you know, remains a high priority for Kraton.  Given our focus on debt reduction, we continue to pursue opportunities to improve our overall capital structure and to optimize the carrying cost of our debt.

 So with that review of the quarter, I'll now turn the call over to Steve Tremblay, our Chief Financial Officer, who'll provide a more in-depth financial review of our first quarter results. Steve?
