Jack P. Williams,  Exxon Mobil Corporation - SVP: Okay. Thank you, Neil. Well, as Neil covered, it was a tough market environment for us this quarter. Overall though, we are pleased with the underlying operating performance of the businesses and, of course, wish that margin environment would have supported the translation of that into higher earnings.
 But as you saw in the Downstream margin plot that Neil showed, the margins were at historically low levels, and our results were in line with that margin environment. The plot also demonstrated the historical volatility of Downstream margins and the wide swings that can happen over pretty short periods of time, and that's why we don't try to predict or forecast margins. Instead, we work to build our businesses to be robust to the swings and why we test new investments across a broad range of prices. Investments we're currently pursuing across all 3 sectors stand up to that testing and our advantage versus industry. This is going to help us manage through this volatility, and it's going to deliver value in markets that remained fundamentally strong.
 Our activities to execute those new investments remain on track and some significant progress so far this year that Neil has mentioned, I'll just reiterate. In the Upstream, we doubled Permian production volumes in the first quarter last year and made 3 new discoveries in Guyana. I feel really good about the strong portfolio of Upstream investments that we have today, which are at the top tier of the industry. And as you know, a strong opportunity pipeline is critical given the depletion nature of the Upstream business.
 In the Downstream, we FID-ed 3 major refining projects, and the other 3 of the 6 projects that I've been talking about are now online. These investments improve the yield profile at strategically important sites, delivering higher-value products that are growing in demand.
 And in Chemicals, we also funded 3 projects, 3 major U.S. Gulf Coast olefin derivative projects, and are making good progress with the Corpus steam cracker, which we expect to FID around mid-year this year, and when we do that, that will be our 12th FID of the 13 investments that underpin the Chemicals growth plan and allow us to maintain a strong position in our performance product markets. And finally, we're continuing to see value from our integrated business model, and we're really pleased that our new Upstream and projects organizations are now up and running.
 So with that, let me provide you activity highlights, starting with the Permian. As you can see on the left-hand graph, we're continuing to track our production outlook. This volumes ramp is supported by a strong well inventory. In fact, by the time we reach 1 million barrels a day of production level in the Permian, we'll have only drilled about half of our current well inventory.
 We're running 46 rigs there, and we'll be ramping up through the year. And this level of rig activity allows us to develop multiple horizons and either full or half sections concurrently, which reduces the risk of parent-child well performance issues as all wells with possible communication will be fracked before any are produced. And development with this method requires blocky acreage and a large rig fleet and a long-term commitment to deal with lumpier production profiles, and we have all 3.
 In addition to this drilling activity, we're building out our unique infrastructure in the Delaware, with the first phase of facilities at the central delivery point in our Southeast New Mexico acreage being ready by year-end. So good progress in the Permian and also in Guyana.
 Last week we announced a new discovery in the Yellowtail-1 well, which, as Neil said, was our 13th discovery on the Stabroek block. You can see in the map on the left that this discovery is in the Turbot area, which is going to be a large development hub similar to Liza. This well along with Haimara and Tilapia discoveries are going to add to the 5.5 billion oil equivalent barrels recoverable resource estimate that we announced earlier this year at our Investment Day (sic) [Investor Day].
 And our drilling continues. Development drilling of 17 wells for producing the first phase of Liza is progressing well and should be completed in the third quarter. The other rigs will continue drilling exploration and appraisal wells, including further drilling on the Hammerhead and Ranger discoveries. The construction of the Liza Destiny FPSO vessels for Phase 1 is being completed in Singapore with planned sail-away this summer and should be in Guyanese waters in the third quarter. A larger Liza Phase 2 development designed to produce 220,000 barrels a day is in the permitting phase and is planned for a 2022 start-up. So lots of activity, exciting new discoveries, really good development progress in Guyana.
 Let me switch gears and talk about a few Downstream project updates. Starting in Singapore, I've spoken about the Singapore resid project before, and it has now been FID-ed. This project is upgrading resid to higher-quality distillates and Group II lube base stocks, which will be unique in industry. No one has ever upgraded heavy fuel oil streams into Group II lube base stocks. This project is taking a notional $60 a barrel product and upgrading it to a $140 a barrel product. It's an industry first and is made possible through proprietary process and catalyst technology. It's the largest of the 6 major refining projects that we have, and due to its technology advantage, it's expected to generate a high-teens return.
 And this project is really a great example of several competitive advantages that we spoke about last March  or back in March. It's made possible by new unique technology. We filed for 35 patents related to the catalyst and novel processes that will be used. And it's a very large project. It's upgrading 90,000 barrels a day of fuel oil, which really moves the needle on site profitability, so clearly, this projects is leveraging our scale. And it's a terrific example of integration. Singapore is our largest integrated site globally. And with this project, we're upgrading both refinery and chemical resid streams with 2 different but complementary technology solutions. In fact, I mentioned this as a Downstream project. You ought to think about this as an integrated Downstream and Chemical project. It significantly improves the competitiveness of the Singapore refinery and reduces the supply cost of our crude cracker below any other liquids cracker in Asia. The start-up is planned for 2023.
 So now let me talk about our project we haven't talked much about, and that's at Fawley. Our project at Fawley is the last of the 6 key refining projects that I introduced to you back in 2018, and it's also now fully funded. This project is more straightforward than Singapore. It leverages advantaged logistics. And like our Rotterdam and Antwerp projects, it's tightly integrated with the Northwest Europe refining and chemical circuit.
 It improves our refining profitability in 2 important ways. First, it upgrades the product slate to better match the U.K. market to a more ultra-low sulfur diesel, more jet fuel, more lower sulfur mogas, which reduces both imports and exports from the site. And second, the project expands Fawley's logistics into the heart of the U.K. market, aligning for increased product flow into our West London Terminal, which services nearby Heathrow Airport. So the combination of these 2 aspects will make Fawley the most efficient and most competitive fuel supply into the greater London market. And this combination also translates into an expected project return in the high teens.
 So again switching gears beyond projects, another activity we've been focused on is the optimization of our entire value chain both in lubricants and in fuels. We've continued to get some questions on our trading activities, so I thought I'd add some context especially since it was a reconciling earnings factor this quarter. On the left is a summary of our global footprint from equity production to refining capacity, to logistics, to our brand and retail sites. Our assets span the globe and the entire value chain. Our objective is to ensure our shareholders capture the full value of that chain from the reservoir to the gas tank and of our footprint from the U.S. to Europe to Asia so no matter where the value is realized along the chain or around the world. So we are using asset-backed trading to best achieve that objective without speculating. For example, closing mogas arbs from Europe to the Americas, we're providing storage of our products  for products when logistics temporarily tighten. We are basically improving the utilization of our global assets and generating solid value from these activities, although sometimes it's difficult to see quarter-on-quarter due to changing mark-to-market impacts from open derivative positions, which was certainly the case this quarter.
 So to wrap up, we're continuing to leverage our competitive advantages of scale, technology, integration, functional excellence and, of course, our high-quality workforce to grow shareholder value. We have made good progress towards our growth plan so far this year with further exploration success and project FIDs. We remain focused on continuously improving our base business while making investments across the value chain to grow earnings and cash flow across a broad range of price and margin environments. James Budge,  Rovi Corporation - CFO: Thank you, Fred and hello, everybody. We grew revenue, as Fred mentioned, to $140 million in Q4, consistent with our updated estimates released in December. In terms of revenue by vertical, our service provider vertical, which is comprised primarily of IPG products and patents license to cable, satellite, and telecom companies grew 13% year-over-year to $70.5 million in the fourth quarter. This growth was driven by the continued conversion of analog to digital, the addition of new international licensees and accelerating growth in our service provider product revenues, which rose 22% year-over-year. The strength in products was achieved by improved pricing on contract renewals, conversions of Cisco Scientific Atlanta SARA's guide to Passport, new Passport applications and advertising.
  Subscribers worldwide receiving a license to our Rovi provided IPG grew 10% from Q4 2009 to 128 million at the end of Q4 2010. Excluding prepaid licensees, primarily Comcast and EchoStar, subscribers were approximately 88 million, up 10% year-over-year. For the year, service provider revenue grew 16% to $267.5 million, up from $230.7 million in 2009. Revenue in our CE vertical which includes guidance products patents and license to device manufacturers and ACP for hardware was $52.5 million in Q4 2010. In Q4 2010, we continued to benefit from double-digit percentage growth in our digital offerings due to increased shipments of IPG-enabled devices and sales of emerging technologies such as our media recognition technologies. However, consistent with the trend, growth was offset by declines in our analog product lines due primarily to certain agreements that slipped from Q3 2009 to Q4 2009 making for a difficult comparison.
  For the full year 2010, CE revenue grew 8.4% to $216.6 million, up from $200 million in 2009, as double-digit percentage growth in our digital solutions were partially offset by declines in our analog revenue, consistent with the last few years and similar to what we expect again in 2011. Revenue for our other vertical which includes data licensing in entertainment was $17.3 million in Q4, up 29% year-over-year. Data licensing continues to grow as we expand our agreements with existing customers and add new customers. For the year, other revenue grew 15.2% to $57.4 million in 2010, up from $48.8 million(Sic-see press release) in 2009.
  Turning to Adjusted Pro Forma profit measures, cost of goods sold totaled $16.8 million or 12% of revenue. SG&A totaled $29.5 million or 21% of revenue and R&D totaled $22.1 million or 15.8% of revenue. Our high operating and earnings margins were due primarily to continued focus on costs as operating expenses declined 2% year-over-year, and interest expense fell due to debt repayment. In terms of Sonic's operating results, Fred will touch on some key highlights shortly and I'd refer you to their 10-Q filed last week for more details.
  Turning to our balance sheet, last week we completed our senior secured credit facility which was upsized in light of very strong demand from $500 million to $750 million. The offering consisted of $450 million of term loan A which bears interest at three months LIBOR plus 250 basis point and $300 million of term loan B financing which pays LIBOR plus 300 basis points with a LIBOR floor of 1%. The term loan A has annual amortization payments of 5% in its first and second years, 10% in the third and fourth years and matures in 2016.
  The term loan B has quarterly amortization payments at 1% annually until maturity in February 2018.As a result of these transactions, we extended the average maturity of our overall debt taking advantage of extremely low interest rates and favorable terms overall, to reduce our cost of capital over time. Having this long-term piece of capital in place will help us continue to retire our more expensive equity linked convertible debt and execute additional share repurchases, plus, restore cash reserves following the Sonic acquisition.
  Our 2011 converts stood at $135 million at the end of December, down from $163 million in September. Since Q4 2010, we paid $115 million to retire $51 million in principal of our 2011 convertible notes which leaves currently $84 million of par value remaining. Pro forma for these repurchases and the new term loan financing, the principal value of our debt stands at $1.3 billion. Cash and investment balances at the end of December were approximately $700 million. Pro forma for the $51 million in convertible debt repurchases subsequent to year end, the new $750 million of debt financing and the anticipated $430 million in cashier marked for the Sonic acquisition and associated expenses, our cash and investments would have been approximately $1 billion at the end of December. We will continue to use excess cash balances to retire the converts and repurchase shares as appropriate.
  Turning to forecasts. As we just provided 2011 standalone estimates in January, we are maintaining those revenue estimates which are [for] between $585 million and $615 million. In addition, given the pending Sonic acquisition, we are now providing combined Company estimates as well. Taking into consideration the Sonic acquisition, we project full year combined Company prospective Adjusted Pro Forma revenue of between $775 million and $825 million versus approximately $723 million in 2010. We expect to provide Adjusted Pro Forma reconciliations for historical results including Sonic Solutions beginning next quarter, after having completed our first partial quarter of combined Company results.
  Our 2011 Prospective Adjusted Pro Forma EPS including Sonic is expected to range between $2.20 and $2.50. Our previous range including Sonic Solutions was $2.35 to $2.65. But after upsizing the term loan we issued last week relative to the initial expectation of $500 million, the associated interest expense will now be higher. Depending on our use of proceeds referenced earlier, we hope to improve upon this range. This range includes the approximate 6 million shares in connection with the Sonic acquisition and all these estimates and historical comparative results assume the Sonic Solutions acquisition closed January 1, 2010.
  In terms of revenue trends by vertical, I'll review the growth estimates we gave at Analyst Day plus updates for Sonic Solutions business line. On the CE side for full year 2010, Rovi standalone finished at $217 million, and we continue to expect flat to low single digit percentage growth for the full year 2011. By way of reminder, while we continue to benefit from flat panel TV industry growth and higher licensing penetration, we also have a downward trend in our analog business which I expect will decline for the fifth consecutive year. We expect the DivX product line, which generated about $73 million in 2010, to roll up into our CE verticals and expect low double-digit growth for this business in 2011. As increased penetration and shipments of emerging device categories like Blu-ray, connected devices, or connected TVs and set-top boxes are partially offset by DVD market decline.
  Turning to service provider, we continue to expect growth in the high teens to low 20% range this year. The positive trend remains the same. We're well positioned for subscriber gains from continued analog to digital conversion plus extensions of customers from patent to product licenses at higher values including more SARA to Passport conversions, international growth and expanded licenses to cover online and mobile fields of use like the Comcast and Cox deals as well as the just announced Cablevision deal which Fred will speak to later.
  In our other category, data licensing continues to benefit from customer additions and expanding licenses with existing customers although this has been largely offset by [ATP] decline. These trends would have left other roughly flat year-over-year according to our standalone estimate. However, we will initially be including Sonic Solutions' other revenue streams in this vertical. These other Sonic revenue streams generated $108 million in non-GAAP Pro Forma revenue in 2010, and we expect them to generate between 25% and 30% growth this year as Roxio ramps in the second half.
  All together, we expect the category we will now refer to as Consumer Software & Other to generate growth in the 15% to 20% range. By way of quarterly [skew] from 2008 to 2010, Rovi standalone averaged 24% of full year revenue in both the first and second quarters, 25% in Q3, and 27% in Q4. Given the high sequential growth of RoxioNow, relative to the 52% we've averaged in years past, we would expect roughly 53% to 54% of revenue to occur in the second half of this year, especially as shipments of RoxioNow enabled-CE devices which generate movie transactions for RoxioNow ramp to form a meaningful installed base. I'd also remind everyone that relative to foreign currency fluctuations, most of our customer agreements continue to be in US dollars and now I'll turn the call back over to Fred. Fred?

Fred Amoroso,  Rovi Corporation - CEO: Thanks, James. As we've just had our Analyst Meeting, I'll briefly review the quarter and recent highlights and then provide a Sonic update. Regarding service providers, despite a slowdown in growth in basic video cable subscribers in the US, our fundamentals remain positive as digital subscribers continue to grow. Plus, we continue to benefit from the robust growth outside of cable, such as through Verizon. As James mentioned, Rovi IPG licensed subscribers grew 10% in Q4. Our subscriber growth also includes international where we're benefiting from both lower relative digital penetration and our growing penetration through new licensees. In addition, we demonstrated progress across key initiatives including broadening our IP licensing program, improving economics on contract renewals and furthering product deployments. On the licensing front we demonstrated significant success with web and mobile licenses. For example, in the US, Cox Communications who has over 5 million subscribers and is a major Passport customer licensed our portfolio for TV Everywhere applications.
  The new agreement includes an expansion of the previous set-top box license into Cox's web and mobile platforms, and will enable Cox to deliver TV across mobile and IP or PC platforms and offer value-added features such as remote record. As just announced today, we also struck a similar web and mobile agreement with Cablevision who has about three million subscribers, almost all of whom are digital. This agreement also covers Cablevision for set-top boxes which were previously licensed through Scientific Atlanta as well as TV Everywhere applications. Cablevision's future set-top box deployments will now generate per subscriber monthly royalties as well their online deployments. Plus, we'll receive our customary advertising revenue share.
  For both Cox and Cablevision, we are pleased with the subscriber-based royalty structures of the agreements, validating our pricing expectations for these types of licenses. We are confident in our ability to sign other service provider web and mobile patent or cross-platform licenses similar to the Comcast, Cox and of course, the Apple agreement. We believe these multi-year agreements go a long way towards further unlocking the potential of the cross-platform guide opportunity which we have referenced in the past as being in the tens of millions incremental dollars annually, thereby contributing to the continued high growth in our service provider vertical. I expect similar agreements forthcoming.
  On the product front as James mentioned we grew our service provider product revenues 22% year-over-year. This was attributable to not only to continued subscriber growth, but also to improved pricing as we renew agreements, deploy new applications and complete more SARA to Passport conversions. These conversions are where we are field upgrading Cisco's Scientific Atlanta boxes which originally shipped with SA SARA guide and for which we collected per unit royalties to our Passport guide for which we will collect recurring monthly per subscriber royalties. As we mentioned previously, two top five operators are replacing SARA guides with Passport through software downloads. These upgrades include such value-added features as our listings data for one of the operators and Show Runner, our integrated VOD guide.
  These two operators combined have around 10 million total pay TV subscribers and we have now converted over several million of the SARA installed base to Passport. I believe this will boost revenue in the $10 million plus range this year. Additionally, we expect both of these operators to deploy our advertising-enabled versions of Passport and one of them has actually already started trialing. Passport 3.5 and Passport 3.6 are the first Passport versions with advertising and we increased our commercial deployments of Passport 3.5 not only in Latin America, but also in Canada last quarter, paving the way for ad-enabled Passport domestically this quarter. We think we'll have several million clients on ad-enabled versions of Passport by year end including in major US markets like San Diego, Phoenix and across the East coast.
  In terms of next generation guides we continue to make progress with our TotalGuide for Service Provider solution. I believe having sufficient services capabilities is currently a constraint but we're working to address this need. Customer interest remains high and we are now currently in licensing discussions with a number of operators and expect wins later in the year. One key value driver, in addition to some of the features we discussed last quarter, is our iPad and tablet capabilities which we demonstrated at CES.We have two different iPad apps.
  The first is what we introduced earlier this month, the Rovi What's on TV app and this app, which is currently available in its initial form, allows users to browse and search local TV listings for a 24 hour period in a graphically-rich, magazine-style layout. The app uses the Rovi Media Cloud to access TV metadata which enables users to find detailed information and images from their favorite shows, movies, and celebrities. The app is merely a beginning for us, however, as we plan to roll out additional iPad and tablet applications throughout the year, with additional capabilities, such as control of TVs and set-top boxes as well as the capability to be white labeled, enabling us to offer the solution to MSOs or CE manufacturers who can't present it as their customer application. It's this type of value-add that operators need to address the over-the-top challenge.
  Turning to CE, we continue to benefit from the digital TV upgrade cycle as volumes rise amid reduced prices and increased functionality. With that said, the flat panel TV market experienced a slowdown throughout the second half of last year, particularly in North America. Overall, DisplaySearch projects flat panel TV growth to slow from 31% last year to around 11% in 2011. But they project connected TV shipments will grow from around 44 million in 2010 to over 64 million this year, to approaching 90 million in 2012, and at a compound annual rate of over 20% through 2014 as manufacturers are moving en masse towards this feature. Our strategy to take advantage of this connected trend over the long term is, of course, through our TotalGuide solution and Rovi Media Cloud services, which addresses the consumer's desire for search, discovery and browsing of content from both broadcast and on-demand sources.
  As we announced at CES, major Tier 1 manufacturers are using our solutions for deployment this year like Samsung who announced a Smart TV platform will utilize Rovi Media Cloud services. As a result of these Tier 1 manufacturers deploying Rovi solutions, we believe it is putting increased pressure on other Tier 1 and Tier 2 manufacturers to follow suit with similar functionality. To address this demand, at CES, we also demonstrated our embedded version of TotalGuide for those that want the full turn key solution that TotalGuide offers. Overall interest is high for our solutions and with these cloud services wins in place, I expect to increase the amount of software and services we supply over time generating significantly more value in the process.
  As for advertising overall, Q4 finished a strong year. We're continuing to make progress, building the foundations of future growth which include increased distribution and enhanced presentation, namely-video enabled ads delivered on advanced guides as well as our improved ability to provide usage metrics to advertisers. As we've said in the past, measurement is critical to demonstrating the appeal of the guides to advertisers which drives distribution and ad dollars our way. We have now turned on measurement in over ten markets and about 200,000 set-top boxes. This measurement data is helpful  excuse me, it's helping to generate wins. For the year, we grew our number of advertisers by over 80%, increased our campaign by 150% and sold over 40% more spots than we did in 2009.
  We were boosted by our expansion beyond our traditional program promotions for the entertainment vertical and into the large conventional advertising market. New advertisers such as Glaxo and Dell continued to expand our conventional footprint. We recently broadened our success in the automotive space where we are featuring Ford ads and to now also include a major foreign auto manufacturer. Many more conventional advertisers are getting interested and I expect significant growth from this category in 2011 and beyond. For example, as of the sixth week of this year, we were 437% higher for bookings than we were in week six of 2010. And while we closed four conventional advertisers in all of 2010, we have already closed 10 conventional advertisers this year.
  While measurement proved instrumental in 2010, 2011 should also benefit from an improved platform experience. The Rovi Media Cloud deal I mentioned earlier with Samsung and others which include our advertising service are proving instrumental in bringing more ad dollars to our business. As a reminder, the ad service in the Rovi Media Cloud allows us to insert advertising into any connected TV, even if a Rovi guide isn't present. This could expand our capability and reach quickly. We had numerous meetings with advertisers at CES who had originally focused on and are currently advertising on our service provider footprint. They are now meaningfully engaging on our CE footprint as well, especially given the buzz around the Sonic acquisition and the positive feedback loop we discussed on the December call. This is in step with our ability to deliver them greater distribution. Samsung will be launching commercially their ad service enabled Smart TVs in March.
  Now that we're expanding our interactive platforms through TotalGuide, Rovi Media Cloud, Passport 3.5 and Passport 3.6, atop our existing i-Guide deployments, I expect to achieve a 50 million household footprint this year which I think is a pretty meaningful audience for advertisers to target. Plus, I'm quite pleased we've begun to make progress towards enabling commerce on our advertisements. Today we announced a partnership with a back-end commerce company to enable consumers to purchase goods directly through their TVs. I'm excited because I believe this broadens our value to advertisers and increases our potential advertising revenue as we will receive a revenue share on commerce transactions. I look forward to providing an update as it rolls out later in the year.
  Overall, I think our announcement of the Sonic Solutions acquisition has generated a significant amount of interest on the part of advertisers, retailers, CE and service provider partners alike and I'm very excited to begin to address these audiences with the combined offering. To review the highlights of the strategic combination, Rovi and Sonic Solutions will be able to power the next wave of digital entertainment offerings with content discovery, delivery and enhanced interactivity capabilities that drive consumer engagement and therefore, also, accelerate our advertising opportunity. Sonic's RoxioNow digital offering enables consumers to readily move content across devices as the rights are managed through the cloud. Rovi's guide technology, in conjunction with our extensive metadata and recommendations engine, is what helps consumers find and discover digital media from a broad range of devices, both over-the-the top and through managed networks.
  In short, we believe we can add value to all constituents in the echo system including service providers, content owners including broadcast design studios, retailers and CE manufacturers. By enriching the user experience, we think consumers will purchase more premium content, generating more demand for our solutions which we believe will drive more traffic through our advertising infrastructure. A rich user experience driving premium content consumption leading to uptake of our solutions across devices and providing targeted advertising capabilities which therefore generates even more premium content transactions. This is a positive feedback loop that drives the strategy behind this deal.
  In terms of recent Sonic Solutions standalone highlights, in the December quarter Sonic announced non-GAAP Pro Forma revenue of $46.3 million. DivX had a strong quarter with non-GAAP Pro Forma revenue of $19.9 million, up 18% year-over-year, driven by demand for emerging products, non-DVD and a trend to higher HD profiles for [DTV], Blu-ray and mobile. Emerging products grew over 100%, as digital television revenue grew approximately 140%. Blu-ray grew 55%, and mobile phone revenue grew over 170%, which benefited in particular from the Samsung Galaxy S offering, all offsetting declines in DVD. Overall, DivX licensed hardware device shipments grew almost 60% year-over-year and is now shipped on approximately 400 million devices.
  The increased uptake of DivX HD profiles is very encouraging and customers renewals are reportedly progressing well. On the RovioNow front, and the platform continues to expand rapidly.At the end of December, over ten million devices cumulatively had shipped with the technology and it is on its way to exceed the previous estimate of 30 million devices by this June. In fact, Sonic has recently added Marvell to the list of chip companies that have adopted the RoxioNow platform, bringing even broader ability to power connected Blu-ray and DTV devices over the next several years. I believe that cumulative device shipments is a very important metric for us now given that it drives the downstream transactions which will take time to cultivate. But earlier results are promising. The increased device penetration is translating into substantial growth in users and movie transactions as device activations grew over 200% year-over-year in January, and these devices are driving increased usage as both units purchased and sales per month rose in the 150% plus range in January 2011 versus January 2010.
  In terms of high profile launches or wins, RoxioNow is now powering the movie stores of Dell, Sears, VIZIO, and Canadian theater chain, Cineplex.Other notable announcements included Intel Media Vault which will allow PC partners such as HP to download HD versions of movies to their PC. We believe this is only the beginning of many more wins to come as the combined platform rolls out. Our integration planning has progressed nicely and I'm very excited to begin executing on our plan.
  As we meet with customers, the message is clear. The customers see the potential of this acquisition and want to engage on how they can begin to factor in the potential combined offering into their purchasing decisions. I look forward to closing the transaction later this week so that we can begin to realize these synergies. At this point I'd like to turn the call back over to Camille so that we can respond to any questions that you might have. Camille?

Hans Jakob Hegge,  Statoil ASA - Executive VP & CFO: Thank you, Peter, and welcome to you all. I'm pleased to present another strong quarter from Statoil. Adjusted earnings before tax was $3 billion and the IFRS result was $3.2 billion before tax. A positive results on a cash flow of $9 billion after tax. We have reduced gearing by 8 percentage points year-to-date. I will revert to the results in a moment.
 The picture on the front page is of Gina Krog, which started to produce this quarter. We have used the downturn to systematically improve our project portfolio. We are working together with our suppliers to realize several large projects. Johan Sverdrup is on schedule, and will be a giant on a global scale. Aasta Hansteen is assembled and ready for field commissioning to start production next year. Njord A is being refurbished to produce for another 20 years.
 Very good progress is also being made on the rest of the portfolio. In addition, 3 plants for development were approved, and we submitted the plan for development Snefrid Nord And we are moving forward with our exploration efforts. Our campaign in the Barents Sea has given us an oil discovery in the Kayak well. This is close to Johan Castberg field. We also had a small discovery in the Blåmann prospect. We are currently drilling the Gemini North prospect before we drill Korpfjell and Koigen Central. These are interesting prospects that may open new areas in the Barents Sea.
 On the macro, we still see volatility in the gas and oil prices. The uncertainty is especially linked to the adherence to production curtailments among the OpEx numbers as well as production of unconventional resources in the U.S. However, our fundamental view remains unchanged as we see drivers for further oil prices going forward. Demand for oil continues to grow, and the low investment levels and new projects during the downturn is expected to have an impact on the supply side, leading to a more balanced oil market.
 The second quarter results have 3 main characteristics. Firstly, they deliver a strong cash flow and a solid result. We have reduced our net debt ratio to 27.5%, down from 35.6% at the end of 2016. Secondly, we continue to have strong operational performance with high regularity and value-adding production. And thirdly, we have high project activity with solid deliveries and we continued to see the results of our efficiency work. We have strengthened our financial position.
 Our dividend policy remains firm. The board has decided to maintain the dividend of $0.2201 per share and will also, this quarter, offer a scrip option with a 5% discount. Just to remind you, the scrip option was announced in February 2016 for a 2-year period ending third quarter this year.
 Then on to the results more in detail. We had adjusted earnings before tax of $3 billion compared to $913 million the same period last year. Strong operational performance with high regularity and high production contributed to the solid result, as well as higher prices for oil and gas. The reversal of a provision related to profit oil in Angola contributed positively to the adjusted result by $754 million. Adjusted earnings after tax was $1.3 billion compared to a loss of $28 million in the same quarter last year.
 The tax rate in the quarter was 57.4%. The low tax rate was mainly a result of the reversal of the provision in Angola. This was partly offset by a higher-than-normal tax rate in MMP due to earnings composition. We realized an oil price of $44.5 per barrel, up from $39.4 the same period last year. Realized gas prices were higher both in Europe and North America by 3% and 65%, respectively, compared to the second quarter last year. We continue to drive down costs, with underlying operating SG&A costs down 8% per barrel compared to the same period 2016.
 Then let's go to the segments. Development and Production Norway delivered adjusted earnings before tax of $1.9 billion, up from $1.2 billion in the same period last year. We continue to see the effort of the continuous improvement work, and the production efficiency the first 6 months is record high. Underlying improvement in OpEx and SG&A per barrel was 11%, measured in NOK year-on-year. Realized liquids prices were 9% higher, and the internal gas transfer price was 36% higher. Liquids production increased by 1%. Gas production increased by 6% year-on-year. The production was the highest second quarter since 2012.
 Development and Production International delivered a result before tax of $876 million. This includes the effect of the reversal of the Angolan provision of $754 million compared to a loss of $506 million in the same period last year. The underlying production growth in the International business was 3%. Cash flow from the International operations amounted to around $19 per barrel after tax. This is at the same level as in our Norwegian upstream business.
 Marketing, Midstream and Processing delivered a pretax result of $292 million compared to $329 million in the second quarter 2016. The main reason for the lower result was weaker contribution from our liquids trading. Good margins and high regulatory at our onshore plants contributed positively to the results.
 Production during the quarter was 1,996,000 barrels per day. Despite high turnaround activity, we experienced high regularity and a strong underlying production growth of 3% year-on-year. Ramp-up from fields like Ivar Aasen and Goliat on the NCS, and Jack/St. Malo and Corrib in our International business contributed positively to the growth. In addition, we produced higher gas volumes as part of our strategy to move gas to take advantage of periods with higher prices. This was 41,000 barrels per day higher than a year ago.
 We are in a robust financial position. As a result of the strong cash flow from operations of $10.8 billion for the first half of this year, the net debt ratio is now at 27.5%, down from 35.6% at the end of last year. We have paid $1.7 billion in taxes, including 3 NCS tax installments; $0.8 billion in dividends, having paid the cash portion of 2 dividend payments; and we have received $0.4 billion from sale of assets.
 Capital investments for the first 6 months were $4.7 billion. This sums up with a net positive cash flow of $4 billion at the end of the first half of 2017. I would like to remind you that we have 3 NCS tax installments in the second half of this year, each at roughly NOK 9.5 billion, reflecting the higher commodity prices in 2017.
 CapEx is expected to be higher in the second half of the year compared to the first half. This is reflecting the higher activity in the third and the fourth quarter. You may also recall that we have entered an agreement to acquire a further 10% of the BMS-8 license in Brazil, and we expect to close this transaction during the second half of 2017.
 I'm rounding off the presentation with our guiding. On the production guidance, we are now saying around 5% organic growth, slightly tighter than the 4% to 5% we gave at our CMU in February. The expected annual production growth from 2016 to 2020 remains unchanged at around 3%. We still expect an additional $1 billion in annual cost improvements in 2017. This is in addition to the $3.2 billion achieved by the end of 2016.
 Our CapEx guiding remains unchanged at around $11 billion. We are reducing our exploration spend from $1.5 billion to $1.3 billion due to strict prioritization and efficiency in our drilling operations.
 With that, I leave it to Peter to take us to the questions.

 I want to first say thank you to team DCP. An incredible credit goes to every employee for delivering some of our best safety, reliability and financial results in what has been an exceptionally challenging environment. Our team and our diversified asset base is strong. Our strategy remains consistent and effective. And the earnings power of the DCP business model is evidenced by our outstanding financial results.
 We generated $220 million of distributable cash flow in the second quarter and $440 million year-to-date, representing our strongest performance since the company was combined with DCP Midstream LLC. As a result of our early and aggressive efforts to optimize cash, we created $54 million of free cash flow in the second quarter, and our bank leverage improved from Q1, now down to a target of 4.0x. Underpinned by our strong year-to-date performance and recent market stabilization, we have reissued our original adjusted EBITDA and DCF guidance, which Sean will discuss shortly.
 During the quarter, volumes across both segments remained stronger than our worst-case scenarios as a result of fewer than anticipated shut-ins and the earlier return of curtailed production. Importantly, we were also able to proactively work with our customers to optimize their netbacks throughout our integrated value chain. This ensured that when shut-in decisions were made, DCP was the service provider of choice and volume stayed on our system, creating a win-win for our customers and for DCP. On our pipes, ethane recovery and opportunistic NGL marketing kept our utilization rates high and our earnings balanced.
 Looking to other highlights in the quarter, with our liquidity now squarely secured through successful capital market execution, our primary financial focus is to utilize our growing free cash flow to delever the company. Our supply-long, capacity-short capital allocation strategy, DCP 2.0 transformation, and integrated footprint will continue to drive efficiencies and generate significant free cash flow throughout 2020 and 2021. Finally, several positive developments in the DJ Basin have completely unleashed the future potential of production, and I look forward to discussing those later in the call.
 On Slide 5, I will outline how a combination of strategic execution and deliberate self-help measures in the first half of this year has helped us overcome a year-over-year adverse price impact of $125 million and while also positioning us well for long-term sustainable success.
 First, and most importantly, our COVID-19 response has prioritized and protected the health and well-being of our workforce. Next, as the downturn took hold, our fully integrated footprint became a critical asset. Approximately 65% of our Q2 adjusted EBITDA was generated by our logistics and marketing segment, demonstrating the earnings power of our pipelines and downstream assets and highlighting the drive of our commercial teams. Not only has this segment produced high quality earnings, but our ability to optimize producer customers' netbacks was critical to keeping volumes on our system and throughput rates high. As a result of our efforts and increased ethane recovery, average Q2 NGL throughput remained flat compared to Q1.
 On top of a great portfolio of assets, we are retaining nearly $900 million of cash on an annualized basis with the sole purpose of strengthening the balance sheet, which has made a critical impact in the first 6 months of this year. Our costs are down $87 million year-over-year, driven by relentless dedication to improving efficiencies in our contract services, consumables, labor and utilities. Our sustaining capital is down $23 million year-over-year due to fewer well connects, risk-based prioritization for projects and deferral of some innovation efforts. And finally, our DCP 2.0 transformation effort allowed us to not only take cost out of the system early, it also enables us to continually optimize margin, enhance flexibility and speed within the organization and perform operations completely remote, including safely operating gas processing plants from employees' homes.
 Our team has achieved significant success and proven our resiliency in navigating this downturn, as demonstrated by the impressive financial and operational excellence outcomes of the past 6 months, including an 11% increase in DCF and a 5% increase in adjusted EBITDA compared to the first half of 2019.
 Now to talk through the details of our Q2 results, guidance, outlook and financial position, I'll turn it over to Sean.

Finally, G&P margins were down $9 million as a result of lower overall volumes in the G&P segment, tied to our Eagle Ford and Midcontinent assets, which were partially offset by increased DJ Basin and Permian volumes.
 I want to close out my Q2 comments by giving a little color of what we're seeing from a volume standpoint early in Q3. July NGL volumes on Sand and Southern Hills have both increased over Q2 average throughput and G&P volumes remain relatively flat versus our Q2 average.
 With our strong first half of the year setting a solid foundation on Slide 7, you'll see that we've reissued our 2020 adjusted EBITDA and DCF guidance, originally given on our February call this year. We've also added a free cash flow measure, defined as distributable cash flow, less distributions and less expansion capital expenditures. With our current distribution coverage sitting at 2.7x for the quarter, free cash flow has been replaced  coverage as a more relevant financial target, highlighting a comprehensive measure of cash flow and indicative of our ability to delever.

 Slide 8 gives some color around our current second half year outlook and potential upside and downside drivers.  Let me now move to the key strategic plan priorities, which are the following, protecting our margins and cash flow generation in mature markets in spite of challenging macro scenarios; keep investing in our business and growth markets; strengthening our balance sheet and optimizing asset portfolio; completing Group's reorganization also through minority buyouts. The consistent approach builds upon the successful strategy we have already implemented in the past, which in particular continue to be focused on a very tight financial discipline.
 Let me now detail each of these priorities to you, starting with cost savings. First I am very proud to state here that we have successfully finalized our Zenith 1 and Enel-Endesa synergies programs during 2012. The remainder part of our previous programs Zenith 2 and One Company project are now embedded into this new one project. According to this new program, which takes as a reference base 2012 total fixed controllable cost, we expect to reach about EUR4b cumulative OpEx reduction by 2017, leveraging major actions on both personnel and external costs.
 Among the most relevant let me list the following actions. First, headcount reductions through Group's reorganization and the full implementation of the One Company project. Two, increase productivity contribution from our labor force. Three, insourcing of activities, i.e. ICT, global services and some in-field operations. Four, capacity closures. Five, best-practices implementation and overall external service costs renegotiation. Let me also underline that two thirds of this program is concentrated on mature markets as it represents a relevant managerial action we leverage to protect our margins.
 Let's now move to CapEx and capacity evolution in our mature markets where the already mentioned negative economic environment coupled with excess of capacity will lead our actions towards efficient capital allocation through the following, maintaining or slightly increasing our investments in distribution; reducing our generation capacity up to 7 gigawatt during the planned period, thus reducing our CapEx in generation by almost 13%; to complement our actions on margin protection we also plan to enter new high value-added services like smart meters in Spain and energy efficiency in Italy.
 Moving to CapEx and capacity evolution in our growth markets, the growing economic framework which features these businesses lead us to increase by 8% our investment in additional capacity in our growth markets as well as in renewables, where we will leverage our geographical and technological diversification. On top of this we will also leverage positive demographic trends and the urbanization process in LatAm to invest in distribution grids.
 Let me be more specific on our growth areas on the following charts.  This will be achieved through the following. In LatAm we'll increase our energy distributed also thanks to our investment in new capacity and in distribution. More specifically as far new capacity in LatAm is concerned let me underline that we can leverage a huge pipeline of more than 11 gigawatt to top up additional capacity during and beyond the industrial plan period. In renewables we will be increasing our output by about 68% versus 2012, adding 4.4 gigawatt of new capacity. As far as Eastern European is concerned we will increase our production by about 10% versus 2012. In Slovakia we will finalize our project of adding 1 gigawatt of new capacity, nuclear capacity, during 2014 and '15 with our Mochovce nuclear plant.
 Let's now move to analyze the third key priority. Strengthening balance sheet is a fundamental part of our strategy as we are committed to maintaining our investment-grade rating. Therefore, we commit ourselves to finalize about EUR6b disposal plan within 2014. This plan will be complemented by a EUR5b program of hybrid financing to be finalized by 2015 with 50% equity content and therefore enhancing the flexibility of our capital structure.
 Specifically the disposals we are planning fall into two categories, assets that are not fully consolidated in our numbers and/or assets we think we can cash-in on their potential now without impacting on our strategy. The businesses we are selling have a limited profitability dilution and cash realized will be used to accelerate the net debt reduction in the first two years of the plan. The above-mentioned initiatives will allow us to defend our credit rating while maintaining the profitability of the Group.
 As far as Group's reorganization is concerned one of the top priorities will continue to be simplifying our Group structure. With specific reference to the LatAm, you know that we have already initiated this process with the ongoing Enersis capital increase. At this regard let me remind you that while we are speaking the offering of both ADS and ordinary shares rights is on course. Once completed this operation will represent the largest rights issue ever recorded in Chile.
 On top of the positive conclusion of the above-mentioned rights issue, during the course of the plan we will go ahead with an overall program of Group's reorganization and minorities buyout aiming at increasing the net income ownership at the parent level from the 65% of today to 78% at 2017. All of this will bring the benefits of enhancing EPS and therefore DPS at the holding level for the benefit of our shareholders.
 Finally on our financial discipline, first let me underline that each every one of us has in mind a key role of the organization to be financially disciplined and everywhere we will do our utmost for that. And let me underline also that the cash coming from Enersis' capital increase will be fully dedicated to minorities buyouts, acquisition and organic growth in the region, in the continent.
 Having said that, let's focus on our accumulative cash flow generation. Through the overall action that I have just outlined our Group will generate accumulative cash flow from operation of in excess of EUR59b, close to EUR60b of which, as I said already, EUR4b will come from our cost savings and efficiencies initiatives. This will fund our global CapEx program amounting to EUR27b, will serve the cost of our debt and will fund dividend payments to both Enel and minority shareholders.
 Cash available for disposals amounting to about EUR14.5b will be dedicated first to debt reduction, which will be our top priority in the first part of the plan period. We had a 30% reduction in the take-or-pay volumes and price thanks  30% reduction in take-or-pay volumes and price reductions. Enel will reopen the discussion with suppliers as provided by the contracts starting in the course of 2013 to further realign the contracts to the evolving market conditions.
 The competitiveness of our coal plants will allow us to increase production volumes above 35 terawatt hours, taking benefits from robust dark spreads.  On Infrastructure & Networks we'll continue to leverage smart technologies to serve our clients with best-in-class operating performances and to dispatch renewables in our medium/low-voltage grid.  In generation solid performance of the economies will trigger our growth in electricity production, leveraging the current pipeline to increase installed capacity over the plan period. In supply we'll be gradually entering the gas business focusing on the final customers particularly in Columbia and Chile. In distribution we will continue on our growth process thanks to the addition of more than 400,000 customers every year.  Turning to financial targets for Iberia and LatAm, again for the obvious reasons of Enersis capital increase I will be prudent in releasing individual targets.  Let's now turn to International targets. In the International division we will continue to put in place efficiency initiatives coupled with incremental capacity, which will protect our profitability in a challenging environment, maintaining our EBITDA at EUR1.5b level all throughout 2015.
 Finally, at our renewables operations the maximization of value will come from increasing installed capacity by 55% in 2017 versus 2012 from 8 gigawatt to 12.4 gigawatt. Growing production by about 70% in 2017 versus 2012. Keeping an effective technological and geographic diversification profile and matched footprint of Enel Green Power.
 Keeping our managing the 23 gigawatt pipeline selectively with 1.8 gigawatt of projects already under construction and ready to be built. Monitoring the evolution of new technologies like concentrated solar thermal dynamic and small biomasses and developing new predictive tools and hybrid plants, and opening new areas of development like Turkey, South Africa, Morocco, Peru and Columbia.
 Our targets in renewables during the plan period will be a CapEx plan confirmed at about EUR6b which will lead to more than 12 gigawatt of total capacity installed by 2017 versus 8 gigawatt as of the end of 2012. A strong increase in EBITDA which will move from EUR1.8b in 2013 to EUR2.4b in 2015. This is mainly due to capacity additions in those areas where the combination of resources availability and need for additional energy create a sustainable platform for renewables regardless of regulatory support.
 Let me now drive you through our overall financial targets starting from our net debt evolution. As it is reported in this chart, in the first two years of our plan period we will remain strongly committed to reduce our net debt level from the EUR43b of 2012 to about EUR37b in 2014. As you will have seen in the course of this presentation, this will be pursued through organic cash flow generation, CapEx control and flexibility as well as asset disposals.
 Let me also remind you that we will implement a EUR5b issuance of hybrid bonds and we expect a net effect of about EUR3b in the cash-in from the Spanish tariff deficit during the period of 2013/2014. By the way, since January 1 up until now we have already cashed in EUR1.6b, in excess of EUR1.6b of that cash deficit  tariff deficit, sorry.
 In the second phase of that plan period we will accelerate our cash flow generation mainly thanks to organic growth initiatives, keeping our 2017 net debt level stable at about EUR36b/EUR37b while completing the minorities buyout program that I've already illustrated to you. All of this will allow the Group to defend its investment-grade credit rating coupled with enhanced overall profitability.
 Now let me comment on our future economic results. During the plan period we'll be focused on EPS growth. At this regard let me underline here that our ordinary net income will rise to EUR4b to EUR5b in 2017 versus EUR3b in 2013 as a result of all the actions embedded in our industrial plan and as you have seen along the presentation. Dividend policy will be confirmed. It is confirmed.
 Now some closing remarks. I would like to close this presentation with what I regard as the key highlights of our plan. Within our mature markets we have a very clear strategy to protect our profitability in the face of a worsening economic scenario. However, the plan also continues the transformation of the Group and sees about 45% of the Group EBITDA in growth markets by 2017.
 Underpinning this strategy we have some clear deliverables which I would like to highlight again. We will increase our cost reduction and efficiency program efforts. We will keep our capital expenditures towards growth markets. We will deleverage our balance sheet through selected disposals and hybrid financing.  Thank you for your attention. Let's go into Q&A session.

 At Bruce Power, the refurbishment programs over the last three years have been expensive, however, they have been driven by the importance of equipment reliability and long-range maintenance strategies. George Assie,  Cameco - SVP Marketing and Business Development: Thank you, Terry, and good day, everyone.
 Looking first at the spot market, activity in the fourth quarter totalled almost 7 million pounds, and that compares to 3 million in the third quarter of 2005, and an average of nearly 13 million pounds in each of the first two quarters of last year.
 Investment funds continued to increase their holdings later in the year and represented about 35% of fourth quarter spot market activity. The relatively strong demand in the fourth quarter, combined with tight supply, continued to support a rising spot price. The year-end industry average price of $36.38 is 15% higher than the third quarter price, and more than 75% higher than the 2004 year-end price of $20.60, and since the beginning of this year, the average spot price increased further by $1.12 to $37.50.
 For the year, spot volumes reached a record high of around 35 million pounds, and that's 75% higher than the average annual volume for the past five years. You may recall that during the early part of 2005, the long-term prices were significantly above spot prices, at times, by more than $5. That gap between spot and long-term prices made it economic for buyers to purchase and hold uranium, resulting in increased spot demand and upward pressure of spot prices. For 2005 as a whole, only about one-third of spot demand was related to purchases to meet near-term utility requirement, with the remainder being discretionary purchases. The discretionary buyers included utilities, building inventory, and investment groups. groups building their uranium holdings. The investment groups, in particular, played a significant role in 2005, accounting for about one-quarter of spot demand.
 At this time, there is little differentiation between spot and long time prices, so today, we do not have that same driver encouraging large discretionary purchases. That could change as we move through 2006, particularly, if long-term contracting volume is strong and long-term prices were to again rise significantly above the spot price.
 Utilities, for the most part, are generally well covered, so we do not see large volumes of spot demand coming from them to cover near-term requirements. Suppliers, including both traders and producers, are likely to come to the spot market to cover upward contract flexibilities under older legacy contracts as buyers under those contract take advantage of the more favorable pricing terms.
 Spot demand will also depend on the level of participation by investment groups and any further inventory adjustments that utilities may make. At this time, we anticipate the 2006 spot demand will return more to the level of the previous five years, somewhere in the order of the 20 million-pound range. On the supply side, uranium stocks appear to remain very tight, and the general view in the market is for spot prices to remain strong during the course of this year.
 Moving now to the long-term market, the average long-term price indicator ended 2005 at $36.13, up 11% from $32.50 at the end of the third quarter. Year-over-year, the long-term market price has increased by about 45%, and since the beginning of this year, it's increased further to $37.
 Term market was extremely active in 2005, with awarded volumes of more than 240 million pounds, not far from tripling the 90 million pounds contracted in 2004, and the record for the industry. This number is likely to increase further as additional contracting information becomes available. Contracts being written in the current market are generally for much longer duration than in the recent past, five to seven years longer, and this trend has contributed to higher volumes.
 In the press release, we provided some guidance on our expected realized prices under different market scenarios, and note, that our average realize price will move closer to the market price by 2008 than is the case today. As we have outlined in the past, Cameco's sells into the long-term market. We have a contract portfolio that contains some legacy contracts that were signed in a much lower priced environment and deliveries under new long-term contracts generally begin several years out in time. Given the history of the uranium market, the nature of contracting for uranium with the focus on term contracting versus spot sales, and the dramatic price rise of almost 250% over the past three years, it is of no surprise that our contract portfolio will lag the market for some time.
 Cameco has been active in the long-term market, securing contracts that will support our ongoing mining operations and new mine developments over the long-term. The commercial terms in these contracts reflect the much improved market conditions we have seen over the past few years, in particularly in 2005.
 We continue to target a 60/40 mix of market-related and fixed prices, and we may adjust that as market conditions evolve. Contracts today are higher fixed and/or floor prices, both of which escalate over time. Volume flexibilities have been dramatically reduced, and ceiling prices, to the extent they are given, provide significant up-side participation.
 To summarize, we're very pleased with the contract portfolio that we're building for the longer term. For 2006, all indications point to another active year for contracting, as utilities continue to look to mitigate the risk of potential future supply shortfalls by securing long-term contracts with reliable primary suppliers. We do not anticipate exceeding the record breaking contracting level of almost a quarter-billion pounds in 2005, but we do expect the demand for long-term contracts to remain quite strong in 2006, and significantly higher than in previous years. At this point, we would estimate that something in the order of 150 million pounds will be contracted in the long-term market in 2006.
 Give that expectation of significant demand in the long-term market and given that relatively few producers with the production capability to supply over the longer term, we expect long-term prices to remain strong in 2006.
 Turning now to the US fixed conversion market, industry average spot prices for both North America and Europe remain steady, and end of 2005, at 11.50 per kilogram, unchanged from the end of the third quarter. That is a increase of about 20% year-over-year, with very little spot US fixed conversion purchased in the fourth quarter of last year.
 In the long-term market, industry average price for North American conversion remain unchanged over the fourth quarter at $12, while the price for European conversion decreased slightly to 12.88 from 13.13 at the end of the third quarter 2005. When comparing to year-end 2004, long-term prices in both the North American and European markets increased by 20% and 12% respectively.
 The demand for US fixed conversion services has continued to be very light during the first month of this year. At the same time, the tightness in U308 supplies in the uranium market has resulted in some sellers trying to de-convert, and by that, we mean they're trying to arrange transactions that will allow them to split US fixed into its component parts, so that they can supply uranium only.
 To complete these transactions, a seller may be willing to take a slight discount on the US fixed conversion, so as to permit them to offer the uranium component. Both of these factors have contributed to some softening in the US fixed conversion price at the end of January, and the average spot price for both North America and Europe now stands at 11.25, and that's down from 11.50. While the long-term price in North America is 11.75, and Europe is 12.63, down from $12 and 12.88 respectively.
 So that concludes my remarks on the market, and with that, I'll turn it back to Gerry.

As we wrap up 2021 and despite the supply chain challenges that we experienced together with our customers, we managed to deliver record net income. Our team delivered once again. We remain optimistic about future opportunities in this business as oil prices remain high, and we continue to promote our new cost-effective product solutions that will improve oilfield operator return on investment and protect their wells.
 We increased our biocide capacity last year and are investing to increase capacity and capability in certain product lines including sulfates, amphoterics and alkoxylates to ensure we can meet higher requirements from our customers. As discussed previously, we are increasing North American capability and capacity to produce sulfates that meet new limits on 1,4-dioxane by the January 2023 regulatory deadline. 1,4-dioxane is a miner byproduct generated in the manufacture of either sulfate surfactants, which are key cleaning and foaming ingredients used in consumer product formulations.
 Through a combination of process optimization and additional manufacturing equipment, Stepan will be prepared to supply customers these sulfates that meet the new regulatory requirements. This project, along with our previous announcement of an alkoxylation production facility at our Pasadena, Texas site are the primary drivers of the forecasted $350 million to $375 million in 2022 capital spending. We are excited about the capability and the future growth that these investment projects will deliver to Stepan Company.
 Tier 2 and Tier 3 customers continue to be a focus of our Surfactant growth strategy. We added 1,400 new customers during 2021, and we will continue serving the strategic market for us.   We feel good about our prospects as we begin the new year. Momentum we experienced during the holidays has continued, as evidenced by our February sales results.

  I'm confident that as long as we stay focused on our mission, as we have three past challenges, we will navigate these new challenges in such a way that will allow us to continue to grow profitably.

  Meanwhile, our e-commerce sales have continued to perform well. Our investments over the past 18 months are paying off with sales growth of 130% during both the fourth quarter and the full year. Our Web now represents about 4.7% of total sales in fiscal 2010, up from 2.5% in fiscal 2009.

  In addition, we made important investments in 2010 that we believe will deliver significant long-term benefits.   Throughout the year we made progress towards our new assortment planning solution with the implementation of merchandise business intelligence. These tools, which will allow us to better plan and micromanage our business, should begin to reduce benefits in 2011 and beyond.
  Also, we made important infrastructure and talent investments across our organization. As we look into 2011 we plan to follow the same investment principles that facilitated our historical growth strategies.
  Looking at the results of the quarter in a bit of detail. Fourth-quarter 2010 net sales increased 17.9% over last year to $156,200,000. This increase was driven by a comp store sales increase of 13% compared to a comp store decrease of 1.7% in the fourth quarter of last year. And the addition of 27 new stores, offset slightly by foreclosures since the end of fiscal fourth-quarter of 2009, which brought our total year-end store count to 400.
  To break down these sales a bit further, same-store sales increased in all geographic areas up between 6% to 15%. Sales from our website continued the strong growth increasing 130% in the quarter.
  All of our departments had positive comps, with the exception of our boy's, which is less than 2% of our sales. The biggest contributors to the comp store sales gains were accessories, men's and footwear department, which combined represent approximately 70% of our sales.
  Comparable store transactions drove our comp store gain, partially offset by a decline in average dollar amount per transaction. Dollars per transaction decreased due to a decline in average unit retail, and to a lesser extent a decrease in units per transaction.
  Gross profit in the fourth quarter of 2010 increased $12,800,000 or 26.6% to $60,900,000 compared to $48,100,000 in the fourth quarter of 2009.
  Gross margin increased 39% in the quarter from 36.3% in the fourth quarter of last year. The 270 basis points increase in gross margin was driven equally by an increase in product margins and leveraging the sales gain over our store occupancy costs.
  Moving to expenses. Total SG&A expenses in the quarter increased $1,800,000, or 5.2% to $36,900,000 from $35,100,000 in the fourth quarter of 2009.   Operating income increased 84.1% to $24 million or 15.4% of sales in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2010, compared to $13 million or 9.8% of sales in last-year's fourth quarter.
  Net income in the fourth quarter increased 70.5% to $15 million, or $0.49 per diluted share from $8,800,000 or $0.29 per diluted share in the prior-year period.
  Turning to the full-year financial results, for the fiscal year ended January 29, 2011 net sales increased 17.5% to $478,800,000, driven by a comparable store sales increase of 11.9% compared to a decrease of 10% in fiscal 2009, and the opening of 27 new stores in the year, offset slightly by the closing of four stores.
  Operating income increased 193.4% to $37,400,000 or 7.8% of sales, driven by an increase in sales, 250 basis points improvement in gross margin, and leveraging SG&A costs during the year.
  Our net income for the fiscal 2010 increased 165.1% to $24,200,000 or $0.79 per diluted share from $9,100,000 or $0.30 per diluted share in fiscal 2009.
  Our fiscal 2010 full-year results include identifiable cost of $2.4 million or approximately $0.05 per diluted share associated with the relocation of our distribution center in Everett, Washington to Corona, California, as well as a charge of $2.1 million or approximately $400,000 per diluted share  I'm sorry, $0.04 per diluted share for the settlement of a previously disposed lawsuit.

This increase in cash was primarily due to the strength of our results over last year, which produced strong operating cash flow, reflected sound working capital management, partially offset by $29,400,000 of capital expenditures, including $12,900,000 spent on our new distribution center in Corona, California, and $3,300,000 related to the purchases of some land that I will speak to in a moment.

On a per square-foot basis inventory increased approximately 4.3% from the end of the last fiscal year. We have continued to do a great job of managing our inventory and growing it at a rate lower than sales.
  Also at January 29, 2011, the Company had no debt, including no outstanding balances on its revolving credit facility.

However, as the process progressed, financial markets became increasingly volatile due to rapidly changing inflation forecasts and rising interest rates. This resulted in a sharp increase in borrowing costs of over 100 basis points, which had a disproportionate near-term impact on the private market interest in our portfolio given its longer weighted average lease term.
 Parties cited these factors and that any proposal would be contingent on significant improvements in financing markets as the main reasons why they ultimately chose not to submit actionable indications of interest for the whole company.
